sentences.zh: 列傳第七十 逆臣 ○秉德本名乙辛 唐括辯 烏帶 大興國 徒單阿里出虎 僕散師恭本名忽土 徒單貞 李老僧 完顏元宜 紇石烈執中本名胡沙虎

translations.literal: Biographies 70: Traitorous Ministers. Bingde, original name Yixin; Tangguo Bian; Wudai; Daxingguo; Tudan Aluchuhu; Pusan Sigong, original name Hu Tu; Tudan Zhen; Li Laoseng; Wanyan Yuanyi; Geshilie Zhizhong, original name Hu Shahu.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 70: Traitorous Ministers — Bingde (born Yixin), Tangguo Bian, Wudai, Daxingguo, Tudan Aluchuhu, Pusan Sigong (born Hu Tu), Tudan Zhen, Li Laoseng, Wanyan Yuanyi, and Geshilie Zhizhong (born Hu Shahu).

sentences.zh: 昔者孔子作《春秋》而亂臣賊子懼，其法有五焉：微而顯，志而晦，婉而成章，盡而不汙，懲惡而勸善。

translations.literal: In antiquity Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, and rebellious ministers and wicked sons were afraid; its method has five aspects: subtle yet manifest, recording intent yet obscure, indirect yet forming chapters, exhaustive yet without defilement, punishing evil and encouraging good.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals, and disloyal ministers and wicked heirs trembled before it. Its artistry rests on five principles: the subtle made clear, intent recorded yet veiled, tactful yet fully formed, thorough yet unsullied, chastising wickedness to encourage virtue.

sentences.zh: 夫懲惡乃所以勸善也，作《逆臣傳》。

translations.literal: For punishing evil is precisely how one encourages good; therefore these 'Biographies of Traitorous Ministers' were composed.
translations.idiomatic: To punish the wicked is to encourage the good — hence these biographies of traitorous ministers.

sentences.zh: 秉德，本名乙辛。

translations.literal: Bingde's original name was Yixin.
translations.idiomatic: Bingde's original name was Yixin.

sentences.zh: 初為西南路招討使，改汴京留守。

translations.literal: At first he was pacification commissioner of the Southwest Circuit; he was transferred to be metropolitan guardian of Bianjing.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as pacification commissioner of the Southwest Circuit, then became guardian of Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起復為兵部尚書，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he entered mourning, then was recalled from mourning to be Minister of War and appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he went into mourning, but was recalled to serve as Minister of War and appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 皇統八年，與烏林答蒲盧虎等廉察郡縣，使還，拜平章政事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Huangtong, together with Wulinadao Puluhu and others he conducted integrity inspections of prefectures and counties; when the mission returned he was appointed Grand Councilor of the Peaceful Administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Huangtong (1148), he joined Wulinadao Puluhu and others on an integrity inspection tour of the prefectures and counties. On his return he was made grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 廷議欲徙遼陽渤海人屯燕南，秉德及左司郎中三合議其事。

translations.literal: At court it was debated whether to relocate the Bohai people of Liaoyang to settle them in the region south of Yan; Bingde and Left Department Director Sanhe deliberated on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated relocating the Bohai people of Liaoyang to garrison the region south of Yan; Bingde and Left Department Director Sanhe were assigned to plan the move.

sentences.zh: 近侍高壽星在徙中，壽星訴于悼後，後以白帝，帝怒，杖秉德而殺三合。

translations.literal: The intimate attendant Gao Shouxing was among those to be relocated; Shouxing appealed to Empress Dowager Dao, and the empress dowager reported it to the emperor. The emperor was angry, had Bingde beaten with the staff, and executed Sanhe.
translations.idiomatic: The intimate attendant Gao Shouxing was slated for relocation. He appealed to Empress Dowager Dao, who told the emperor. Enraged, the emperor had Bingde beaten and executed Sanhe.

sentences.zh: 是時熙宗在位久，悼後幹政，而繼嗣未立，帝無聊不平，屢殺宗室，箠辱大臣。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xizong had been on the throne a long time; Empress Dowager Dao interfered in government, and no heir had been established. The emperor was restless and discontented, repeatedly killing members of the imperial clan and beating and humiliating great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Xizong had reigned for many years. Empress Dowager Dao dominated politics, yet no heir had been named. Restless and ill at ease, the emperor repeatedly killed princes of the blood and flogged his senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 秉德以其故懷忿，乃與唐括辯、烏帶等謀廢立。

translations.literal: Bingde harbored resentment on this account and therefore joined Tangguo Bian, Wudai, and others in plotting deposition and enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Bingde nursed a grudge over this and joined Tangguo Bian, Wudai, and others in a plot to depose the emperor and set up another.

sentences.zh: 烏帶以其謀告海陵，海陵乃與秉德謀弑熙宗。

translations.literal: Wudai reported their plot to Hailing, and Hailing thereupon joined Bingde in plotting to assassinate Emperor Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: Wudai betrayed the plot to Hailing, who then conspired with Bingde to murder Emperor Xizong.

sentences.zh: 皇統九年十二月九日，遂與唐括辯、烏帶、忽土、阿里出虎、大興國、李老僧、海陵妹夫特廝，弑熙宗於寢殿。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the twelfth month of the ninth year of Huangtong, together with Tangguo Bian, Wudai, Hu Tu, Aluchuhu, Daxingguo, Li Laoseng, and Hailing's brother-in-law Tesi, they assassinated Emperor Xizong in the sleeping hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the twelfth month of Huangtong 9 (1149), they murdered Emperor Xizong in the sleeping hall — Tangguo Bian, Wudai, Hu Tu, Aluchuhu, Daxingguo, Li Laoseng, and Hailing's brother-in-law Tesi among them.

sentences.zh: 秉德初意不在海陵，已弑熙宗，未有所屬，忽土奉海陵坐，秉德等皆拜稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Bingde's original intent had not been for Hailing; once Emperor Xizong was killed and no one had yet been chosen, Hu Tu seated Hailing, and Bingde and the others all bowed and hailed long life.
translations.idiomatic: Bingde had not originally meant to elevate Hailing. After the murder, with no successor yet chosen, Hu Tu seated Hailing on the throne, and Bingde and the rest all bowed and cried "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 殺曹國王宗敏、左丞相宗賢。

translations.literal: They killed Prince of Cao Zongmin and Left Chief Councilor Zongxian.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Prince of Cao Zongmin and the left chief councilor Zongxian.

sentences.zh: 時秉德位在海陵上，因被杖怨望謀廢立，而海陵因之以為亂。

translations.literal: At that time Bingde's rank was above Hailing's; because he had been beaten with the staff he harbored resentment and plotted deposition and enthronement, and Hailing used this as grounds to accuse him of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Bingde still outranked Hailing. Nursing resentment from his beating, he again plotted to depose and replace him — and Hailing seized on this as proof of sedition.

sentences.zh: 既立，以秉德為左丞相，兼侍中、左副元帥，封蕭王，賜鐵券，與錢二千萬、絹一千匹、馬牛各三百、羊三千。

translations.literal: Once enthroned, he appointed Bingde left chief councilor, concurrently Palace Attendant and left vice commander-in-chief, enfeoffed him as Prince of Xiao, granted an iron certificate of mercy, and gave him twenty million in cash, a thousand bolts of silk, three hundred horses and three hundred oxen each, and three thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the throne, Hailing made Bingde left chief councilor, palace attendant, and left vice commander-in-chief, enfeoffed him as Prince of Xiao, granted an iron certificate, and rewarded him with twenty million cash, a thousand bolts of silk, three hundred horses and oxen apiece, and three thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 久之，為烏帶所譖，出領行台尚書省事。

translations.literal: After some time he was slandered by Wudai and sent out to head the Branch Secretariat of the Mobile Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wudai slandered him, and he was sent out to head the mobile imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時秉德方在告，亟召之，限十日內發行。

translations.literal: At that time Bingde was on leave for mourning; he was urgently summoned and ordered to set out within ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Bingde was then on bereavement leave; he was urgently recalled and told to depart within ten days.

sentences.zh: 會海陵欲除太宗諸子，並除秉德，以秉德首謀廢立，及弑熙宗下即勸進，銜之。

translations.literal: It happened that Hailing wished to eliminate the sons of Emperor Taizong of the Jin and also eliminate Bingde, because Bingde had been the first to plot deposition and enthronement and, right after assassinating Emperor Xizong, had urged Hailing to take the throne — Hailing bore a grudge against him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was moving to eliminate Taizong's sons and meant to remove Bingde as well. Bingde had led the plot to depose Xizong, yet after the murder had pressed Hailing to take the throne — a grudge Hailing never forgot.

sentences.zh: 烏帶因言秉德與宗本謀反有狀，曰：「昨來秉德曾于宗本家飲酒，海州刺史子忠言，秉德有福，貌類趙太祖，秉德偃仰笑受其言。

translations.literal: Wudai then said that Bingde's conspiracy with Zongben to rebel had clear evidence, stating: "Recently Bingde drank at Zongben's house. Zizhong, prefect of Haizhou, said Bingde had good fortune and his appearance resembled Emperor Taizu of Song; Bingde leaned back and laughed, accepting his words.
translations.idiomatic: Wudai reported that Bingde and Zongben had clearly plotted rebellion. He said: "The other day Bingde drank at Zongben's house. Zizhong, prefect of Haizhou, told him he was blessed and looked like Emperor Taizu of Song. Bingde leaned back and laughed, pleased with the flattery.

sentences.zh: 臣妻言秉德妻嘗指斥主上，語皆不順。

translations.literal: My wife says Bingde's wife once pointed at and reviled the sovereign; her words were all disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: My wife says Bingde's wife once reviled the sovereign to his face — every word was seditious.

sentences.zh: 及秉德與宗本相別時，指斥尤甚，且謂歷數有歸。

translations.literal: When Bingde and Zongben took leave of each other, the reviling was especially severe, and they said the mandate of dynastic fortune had found its destination.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingde and Zongben parted, the abuse was even worse — they declared that the mandate had passed to them.

sentences.zh: 秉德招刑部侍郎漫獨曰'已前曾說那公事，頗記憶否'。

translations.literal: Bingde summoned Vice Minister of Punishments Mandu and said, 'We spoke before about that business — do you remember it rather well?'
translations.idiomatic: Bingde called Vice Minister of Punishments Mandu aside and asked, "We discussed that matter before — do you still remember?"

sentences.zh: 漫獨曰，'不存性命事何可對眾便說'。

translations.literal: Mandu said, 'A matter that concerns one's very life — how could one speak of it openly before the assembly?'
translations.idiomatic: Mandu replied, "A matter of life and death — how could I speak of it openly before everyone?"

sentences.zh: 似此逆狀甚明。」

translations.literal: Rebellious conduct such as this is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: Treason such as this is plain enough.

sentences.zh: 海陵遣使就行台殺秉德，並殺前行台參知政事烏林答贊謀。

translations.literal: 」Hailing sent envoys to the mobile secretariat to kill Bingde, and also killed the former vice grand councilor of the mobile secretariat, Wulinadao Zanmou.
translations.idiomatic: 」Hailing sent agents to the mobile secretariat to execute Bingde, along with the former vice grand councilor Wulinadao Zanmou.

sentences.zh: 贊謀妻，秉德乳母也。

translations.literal: Zanmou's wife was Bingde's wet nurse.
translations.idiomatic: Zanmou's wife had been Bingde's wet nurse.

sentences.zh: 初，贊謀與前行台左丞溫敦思忠同在行台，思忠黷貨無厭，贊謀薄之，由是有隙，故思忠乘是並誣贊謀及其子，殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zanmou and the former left vice director of the mobile secretariat, Wendun Sizhong, had served together at the mobile secretariat. Sizhong was insatiably corrupt in taking bribes; Zanmou looked down on him, and from this a rift arose. Therefore Sizhong seized the opportunity to falsely accuse Zanmou and his son together and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zanmou had served at the mobile secretariat alongside its former left vice director Wendun Sizhong, who was insatiably corrupt. Zanmou despised him, and they fell out. Sizhong seized the moment to frame Zanmou and his son and had them killed.

sentences.zh: 贊謀不肯跪受刑，行刑者立而縊殺之。

translations.literal: Zanmou refused to kneel to receive punishment; the executioners strangled him while he stood.
translations.idiomatic: Zanmou would not kneel for execution; the executioners strangled him standing.

sentences.zh: 海陵以贊謀家財奴婢盡賜思忠。

translations.literal: Hailing gave all of Zanmou's family property and slaves and servants to Sizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing gave all of Zanmou's property and household slaves to Sizhong.

sentences.zh: 秉德與烏帶以口語致怨，既死遂並殺其弟特里、颭里，及宗翰子孫，死者三十餘人，宗翰之後遂絕。

translations.literal: Bingde and Wudai had incurred mutual resentment through words; once Bingde was dead they then together killed his younger brothers Teli and Zhali, as well as the descendants of Zonghan — more than thirty persons died, and Zonghan's line was thus extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Bingde and Wudai had quarreled bitterly. After Bingde's death they killed his younger brothers Teli and Zhali and wiped out Zonghan's descendants — more than thirty dead, and Zonghan's line was ended.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，追復秉德官爵，贈儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he posthumously restored Bingde's offices and titles and granted him the posthumous rank of Director with Threefold Parity.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong came to the throne, he posthumously restored Bingde's offices and enfeoffed him with the rank of Director with Threefold Parity.

sentences.zh: 初，撒改薨，宗翰襲其猛安親管謀克。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sagai died, Zonghan inherited his personally administered military district of meng'an and mouke.
translations.idiomatic: When Sagai died, Zonghan inherited his personally administered meng'an and mouke district.

sentences.zh: 秉德死，海陵以賞烏帶，傳其子兀答補，大定六年，世宗憫宗翰無後，詔以猛安謀克還撒改曾孫盆買，遣使改葬撒改、宗翰于山陵西南二十里，百官致奠，其家產給近親以奉祭祀。

translations.literal: When Bingde died, Hailing gave the reward to Wudai, and it passed to his son Wudabu. In the sixth year of Dading, Emperor Shizong pitied that Zonghan had no descendants and decreed that the meng'an and mouke be returned to Sagai's great-grandson Penmai; he sent envoys to reinter Sagai and Zonghan twenty li southwest of the imperial tombs, the hundred officials offered sacrifices, and their family property was given to close kin to maintain the ancestral rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Bingde's death Hailing rewarded Wudai with the district, which passed to his son Wudabu. In Dading 6 (1166), pitying that Zonghan had no heirs, Shizong returned the meng'an and mouke to Sagai's great-grandson Penmai, reburied Sagai and Zonghan twenty li southwest of the imperial tombs with full rites, and assigned their estates to close kin for ancestral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 秉德既死，其中都宅第，左副元帥杲居之。

translations.literal: After Bingde died, his residence at the Central Capital was occupied by the left vice commander-in-chief, Gao.
translations.idiomatic: After Bingde's death his mansion at the Central Capital was taken over by the left vice commander-in-chief Gao.

sentences.zh: 杲死，海陵遷都，迎其嫡母徒單氏居之。

translations.literal: When Gao died, Hailing moved the capital and brought his own birth mother, the Lady Tudan, to live there.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao died, Hailing moved the capital and installed his birth mother, Lady Tudan, in the house.

sentences.zh: 徒單遇害，世宗惡其不祥，施為佛寺。

translations.literal: Tudan met with violent death; Emperor Shizong disliked its ill omen and had it converted into a Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tudan was murdered there. Shizong found the place ill-omened and turned it into a Buddhist temple.

sentences.zh: 唐括辯

translations.literal: Tangguo Bian
translations.idiomatic: Tangguo Bian

sentences.zh: 唐括辯，本名斡骨剌。

translations.literal: Tangguo Bian's original name was Wogula.
translations.idiomatic: Tangguo Bian's original name was Wogula.

sentences.zh: 尚熙宗女代國公主，為駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Emperor Xizong's daughter, Princess of Daiguo, and served as Commandant of Cavalry-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He married Emperor Xizong's daughter, Princess of Daiguo, and became commandant of cavalry-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 累官參知政事、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Vice Grand Councilor and Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice grand councilor and left vice director of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與右丞相秉德謀廢立，而烏帶以告海陵，海陵謂辯曰：「我輩不以匡救，旦暮且及禍。

translations.literal: Together with the right chief councilor Bingde he plotted deposition and enthronement, but Wudai reported it to Hailing. Hailing said to Bian: "If we do not act to rescue the situation, morning or evening we shall meet with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted with the right chief councilor Bingde to depose the throne, but Wudai informed Hailing. Hailing told Bian: "If we do not intervene, disaster will strike us any day now.

sentences.zh: 若行大事，誰可立者？」

translations.literal: If we undertake a great affair, who can be enthroned?
translations.idiomatic: If we raise a coup, whom should we set up?

sentences.zh: 辯曰：「無乃胙王常勝乎？」

translations.literal: 」Bian said: "Might it not be the Prince of Zu, Changsheng?
translations.idiomatic: 」Bian said: "What of the Prince of Zu, Changsheng?

sentences.zh: 海陵問其次，辯曰：「鄧王子阿楞。」

translations.literal: 」Hailing asked who came next; Bian said: "Aleng, son of the Prince of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: 」Hailing pressed for the next choice. Bian said: "Aleng, son of the Prince of Deng.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「阿楞屬疏，安得立。」

translations.literal: 」Hailing said: "Aleng's line is remote — how could he be enthroned?
translations.idiomatic: 」Hailing said: "Aleng is too far from the line — he cannot be enthroned.

sentences.zh: 辯曰：「公豈有意邪？」

translations.literal: 」Bian said: "My lord, do you perhaps have the intent yourself?
translations.idiomatic: 」Bian said: "Do you mean yourself?

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「若不得已，捨我其誰。」

translations.literal: 」Hailing said: "If there is no alternative, who but me?
translations.idiomatic: 」Hailing said: "If it must be done, who but me?

sentences.zh: 於是，旦夕相與密謀。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon day and night they secretly plotted together.
translations.idiomatic: 」From then on they plotted together day and night.

sentences.zh: 護衛將軍特思疑之，以告悼後曰：「辯等因間每竊竊偶語，不知議何事。」

translations.literal: The guard general Tesi suspected them and reported to Empress Dowager Dao: "Bian and the others, whenever they have a chance, always whisper to each other in private — one does not know what they are discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Guard general Tesi grew suspicious and told Empress Dowager Dao: "Bian and his circle keep whispering together whenever they can — no one knows what they are plotting.

sentences.zh: 悼後以告熙宗，熙宗怒，召辯責之曰：「爾與亮謀何事，將如我何。」

translations.literal: 」The empress dowager reported it to Emperor Xizong. Xizong was angry, summoned Bian, and rebuked him: "What affair are you and Liang plotting — what do you intend to do to me?
translations.idiomatic: 」The empress dowager told Emperor Xizong. Enraged, Xizong summoned Bian and demanded: "What are you and Liang plotting — what do you mean to do to me?

sentences.zh: 杖而遣之。

translations.literal: 」He had him beaten with the staff and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: 」He had him beaten and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 自是謀益甚。

translations.literal: From this time the plotting grew all the more intense.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the conspiracy only deepened.

sentences.zh: 十二月九日，代國公主為其母悼后作佛事，居寺中，故海陵、秉德等俱會於辯家。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the twelfth month, Princess of Daiguo was performing Buddhist rites for her mother Empress Dowager Dao and was staying in a temple; therefore Hailing, Bingde, and the others all gathered at Bian's house.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth of the twelfth month, Princess of Daiguo was holding Buddhist rites for Empress Dowager Dao at a temple. Hailing, Bingde, and the others therefore met at Bian's house.

sentences.zh: 至夜，辯等以刀藏衣下，相隨入宮，門者以辯駙馬不疑，皆內之。

translations.literal: When night came, Bian and the others hid knives beneath their robes and followed one another into the palace. The gatekeepers, because Bian was the emperor's son-in-law, did not suspect them and let them all enter.
translations.idiomatic: At night Bian and the others concealed knives in their robes and entered the palace together. The gatekeepers, trusting Bian as the emperor's son-in-law, admitted them all.

sentences.zh: 至殿門，直宿護衛覺之，辯舉刀呵之使無動。

translations.literal: At the hall gate the guards on night duty noticed them; Bian raised his knife and shouted at them not to move.
translations.idiomatic: At the hall gate the night guards noticed them. Bian brandished his knife and ordered them not to move.

sentences.zh: 既弑熙宗，立海陵，辯為尚書右丞相兼中書令，封王，賜錢二千萬、絹千匹、馬牛各三百、羊三千、並鐵券。

translations.literal: After assassinating Emperor Xizong and enthroning Hailing, Bian was made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as prince, and granted twenty million in cash, a thousand bolts of silk, three hundred horses and three hundred oxen each, three thousand sheep, and an iron certificate of mercy.
translations.idiomatic: After murdering Xizong and enthroning Hailing, Bian was made right vice director of the imperial secretariat and director of the secretariat, enfeoffed as prince, and rewarded with twenty million cash, a thousand bolts of silk, three hundred horses and oxen apiece, three thousand sheep, and an iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 進拜左丞相。

translations.literal: He was advanced to left chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 父彰德軍節度使重國，遷東平尹。

translations.literal: His father Chongguo, military commissioner of the Zhangde Army, was transferred to be prefect of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chongguo, military commissioner of the Zhangde Army, was transferred to prefect of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 初，辯與海陵謀逆，辯嘗言其家奴多可用者，海陵固已懷之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bian and Hailing plotted rebellion, Bian had once said that many of his household slaves could be put to use; Hailing had already harbored suspicion of this.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian and Hailing first plotted treason, Bian had boasted that many of his household slaves were useful men — a remark Hailing never forgot.

sentences.zh: 及行弑之夕會於辯家，待興國出宮，辯因設饌，眾皆恇懼不能食，辯獨飽食自若，海陵由此知其忮忍，畏忌之，及即位，嘗與辯觀太祖畫像，海陵指示辯曰：「此眼與爾相似。」

translations.literal: On the night they carried out the assassination they met at Bian's house, waiting for Daxingguo to come out of the palace. Bian set out a feast; everyone was fearful and could not eat, but Bian alone ate his fill as if at ease. From this Hailing knew how cruel and ruthless he was and came to fear and be wary of him. After taking the throne, he once viewed a portrait of Taizu with Bian; Hailing pointed and said to Bian: "These eyes resemble yours.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the murder they gathered at Bian's house, waiting for Daxingguo to leave the palace. Bian laid out a feast. The others were too terrified to eat; Bian alone ate his fill without concern. Hailing saw how ruthless he was and grew afraid of him. After his enthronement he once viewed Taizu's portrait with Bian and said, pointing: "These eyes look like yours.

sentences.zh: 辯色動，海陵亦色動，由是疑辯，益忌之。

translations.literal: 」Bian's expression changed, and Hailing's expression also changed; from this he suspected Bian and feared him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: 」Bian's face changed — and so did Hailing's. From that moment Hailing suspected him and feared him all the more.

sentences.zh: 及與蕭裕謀致宗本罪，並致辯嘗與宗本謀反，即殺之。

translations.literal: When he joined Xiao Yu in plotting to bring charges against Zongben, he also brought charges that Bian had once conspired with Zongben to rebel, and immediately killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When he and Xiao Yu framed Zongben, he also charged that Bian had once plotted rebellion with him — and had Bian killed at once.

sentences.zh: 重國坐奪官，正隆二年，起為沂州防禦使，改清州防禦使。

translations.literal: Chongguo was stripped of office on account of the case. In the second year of Zhenglong he was recalled to serve as defense commissioner of Yizhou, then transferred to defense commissioner of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chongguo lost his office because of the case. In Zhenglong 2 (1157) he was recalled as defense commissioner of Yizhou, then transferred to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 大定初，重國與徒單拔改俱以政跡著聞，歷安國、彰化、橫海軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading, Chongguo and Tudan Bagai were both renowned for their administrative achievements, and he successively served as military commissioner of the Anguo, Zhanghua, and Henghai armies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dading era Chongguo and Tudan Bagai were both noted for distinguished administration; he served in turn as military commissioner of the Anguo, Zhanghua, and Henghai armies.

sentences.zh: 後辯子孫上書，言辯死天德間，祖重國亦坐追削。

translations.literal: Later Bian's descendants submitted a memorial stating that Bian had died during the Tiande era and that his grandfather Chongguo had also been posthumously stripped on account of the case.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bian's descendants petitioned that Bian had died in the Tiande era and that their grandfather Chongguo had also been posthumously stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 正隆初，重國已復官職，乞追復辯官爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenglong, Chongguo had already had his offices restored and requested posthumous restoration of Bian's offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: By early Zhenglong Chongguo had regained his offices and asked that Bian's rank be posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 是時，海陵已降為庶人，以辯與弑逆，不許。

translations.literal: At that time Hailing had already been reduced to commoner status; because Bian had participated in regicide, the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: By then Hailing had been reduced to commoner status, but because Bian had joined the regicide, the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 烏帶妻唐括氏淫泆，舊與海陵通，又私其家奴閻乞兒，秉德嘗對熙宗斥其事，烏帶銜之未發也。

translations.literal: Wudai's wife, the Lady Tangguo, was licentious; she had formerly had relations with Hailing and also secretly took their household slave Yan Qi'er. Bingde had once denounced the affair to Emperor Xizong in his presence; Wudai harbored resentment but had not yet acted on it.
translations.idiomatic: Wudai's wife, Lady Tangguo, was dissolute — she had once been Hailing's lover and later took their slave Yan Qi'er as well. Bingde had denounced this to Emperor Xizong in open court. Wudai nursed a grudge but had not yet struck.

sentences.zh: 時海陵多忌，會有疾，少間，烏帶遂誣奏：「秉德有指斥語，曰：主上數日不視朝，若有不諱，誰當繼者？

translations.literal: At that time Hailing was very suspicious. It happened that he fell ill and recovered after a short interval; Wudai then submitted a false accusation: "Bingde had words of reviling, saying: The sovereign has for several days not held court — if something untoward should occur, who ought to succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was deeply suspicious. When he fell briefly ill, Wudai lodged a false report: "Bingde spoke treasonously, saying: 'The sovereign has not held court for days — if the worst should happen, who will succeed him?

sentences.zh: 臣曰：主上有皇子。

translations.literal: I said: The sovereign has imperial sons.
translations.idiomatic: I said: 'The sovereign has sons.'

sentences.zh: 秉德曰：嬰兒豈能勝天下大任，必也葛王乎」。

translations.literal: Bingde said: How could an infant bear the great burden of all under Heaven — surely it must be the Prince of Ge?"
translations.idiomatic: Bingde said: 'How could an infant bear the empire — surely it must be the Prince of Ge?'"

sentences.zh: 海陵以為實然，故出秉德，已而殺之，以秉德世襲猛安謀克授烏帶。

translations.literal: Hailing believed this to be true and therefore sent Bingde out of the capital; afterward he killed him and gave Bingde's hereditary meng'an and mouke to Wudai.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing believed it and sent Bingde out of court, then killed him and gave Wudai Bingde's hereditary meng'an and mouke.

sentences.zh: 進右丞相。

translations.literal: He was advanced to right chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 烏帶與宗本有親，海陵以烏帶告秉德事，故宗本之禍烏帶獨免，遂以秉德千戶謀克及其子婦家產盡賜之。

translations.literal: Wudai was related to Zongben by kinship. Because Hailing had used Wudai to report the affair of Bingde, when the disaster befell Zongben Wudai alone was spared; thereupon Bingde's thousand-household mouke and the family property of his son and daughter-in-law were all given to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wudai was kin to Zongben. Because he had informed on Bingde, he alone escaped when Zongben fell — and received Bingde's thousand-household mouke and all the property of his son and daughter-in-law.

sentences.zh: 進司空、左丞相、兼侍中。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of Works, left chief councilor, and concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of works, left chief councilor, and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 居數月，烏帶早朝，以日陰晦將雨，意海陵不視朝，先趨出朝，百官皆隨之去。

translations.literal: After several months, at an early court session Wudai, because the sun was dim and overcast and rain was expected, supposed that Hailing would not hold court and hurried out of court first; the hundred officials all followed him and left.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later, at an early session Wudai saw the sky dark and thought rain would keep Hailing from court. He left first — and the whole assembly followed.

sentences.zh: 已而海陵御殿，知烏帶率百官出朝，惡之，遂落司空，出為崇義軍節度使。

translations.literal: Presently Hailing took the throne in the hall and learned that Wudai had led the hundred officials out of court; he was displeased and therefore stripped him of the rank of Minister of Works and sent him out as military commissioner of the Chongyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing then took the throne and learned that Wudai had led the officials away. Offended, he stripped him of the rank of minister of works and sent him out as military commissioner of the Chongyi Army.

sentences.zh: 後海陵思慕唐括容色，因其侍婢來候問起居，海陵許立為後，使殺烏帶。

translations.literal: Later Hailing yearned for Tangguo's beauty; because her serving maid came to inquire after his health, Hailing promised to make her empress and had Wudai killed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hailing pined for Tangguo's beauty. When her maid came to inquire after his health, he promised to make her empress — and had Wudai killed.

sentences.zh: 海陵詐為烏帶哀傷，使其子兀答補佩金符乘驛赴喪，追封為王，仍詔有司送其靈車，賜絹三百為道途費。

translations.literal: Hailing pretended to grieve for Wudai, had his son Wudabu wear the gold tally and travel by post-horse relay to attend the funeral, posthumously enfeoffed him as prince, and still decreed that the relevant offices send his funeral carriage and grant three hundred bolts of silk for travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing feigned grief, sent Wudai's son Wudabu with the gold tally by relay to the funeral, posthumously enfeoffed Wudai as prince, and ordered officials to escort the bier and grant three hundred bolts of silk for the journey.

sentences.zh: 納唐括于宮中，封貴妃。

translations.literal: He took Tangguo into the palace and enfeoffed her as Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: He took Tangguo into the palace and made her noble consort.

sentences.zh: 兀答補襲猛安謀克。

translations.literal: Wudabu inherited the meng'an and mouke.
translations.idiomatic: Wudabu inherited the meng'an and mouke.

sentences.zh: 大定六年，以猛安謀克還撒改曾孫，以阿魯補謀克授兀答補，終同知大興尹。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dading the meng'an and mouke were returned to Sagai's great-grandson; the mouke of Alubu was given to Wudabu in exchange, and he ultimately served as vice prefect of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 6 the meng'an and mouke were returned to Sagai's great-grandson; Wudabu received the Alubu mouke in compensation and eventually became vice prefect of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 子瑭，本名烏也阿補，以曾祖阿魯補功，充筆硯祗候。

translations.literal: His son Tang, original name Wuye'abu, on account of his great-grandfather Alubu's merit served as brush-and-ink attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tang, born Wuye'abu, served as brush-and-ink attendant on account of his great-grandfather Alubu's merit.

sentences.zh: 大興國

translations.literal: Daxingguo
translations.idiomatic: Daxingguo

sentences.zh: 大興國，事熙宗為寢殿小底，權近侍局直長，最見親信，未嘗去左右。

translations.literal: Daxingguo served Emperor Xizong as a petty attendant of the sleeping hall, acting director of the Bureau of Intimate Attendance, and was most trusted — he never left the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Daxingguo served Emperor Xizong as a petty attendant of the sleeping hall and acting director of the Bureau of Intimate Attendance. He was the emperor's most trusted attendant and never left his side.

sentences.zh: 每逮夜，熙宗就寢，興國時從主者取符鑰歸家，主者即以付之，聽其出入以為常。

translations.literal: Each night when Emperor Xizong went to bed, Daxingguo would take the tally-keys from the chief attendant and return home; the chief attendant would at once hand them over to him, and his coming and going was treated as routine.
translations.idiomatic: Each night when Xizong retired, Daxingguo would take the tally-keys from the chief attendant and go home — the keys were routinely handed to him, and his comings and goings were taken for granted.

sentences.zh: 皇統九年，海陵生日，熙宗使興國以宋司馬光畫像及他珍玩賜海陵，悼後亦以物附賜，熙宗不悅，杖興國一百。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Huangtong, on Hailing's birthday, Emperor Xizong had Daxingguo present to Hailing a portrait of Sima Guang of Song and other precious curios as gifts; Empress Dowager Dao also sent gifts to accompany the presentation. Emperor Xizong was displeased and had Daxingguo beaten one hundred strokes with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 9, on Hailing's birthday, Xizong sent Daxingguo to present Hailing with a portrait of Sima Guang of Song and other treasures. Empress Dowager Dao added gifts of her own. Xizong was angry and had Daxingguo beaten a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 海陵謀弑，意先得興國乃可伺間入宮行大事，且度興國無罪被杖必有怨望心，可乘此說之，乃因李老僧結興國。

translations.literal: Hailing plotted assassination and thought that he must first win over Daxingguo before he could watch for an opportunity to enter the palace and carry out the great affair; moreover he reckoned that Daxingguo, having been beaten without guilt, must harbor resentment, which could be used to persuade him — therefore through Li Laoseng he connected with Daxingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing plotted murder and knew he must win Daxingguo first — only then could he seize a moment to enter the palace. He reckoned that Daxingguo, beaten without cause, must bear a grudge — and approached him through Li Laoseng.

sentences.zh: 既而，知無異心可與謀，乃召至臥內，令解衣，欲與之俱臥，意有所屬者。

translations.literal: Presently, knowing he had no disloyal intent with whom to plot, he summoned him into his sleeping quarters, ordered him to remove his clothes, and wished to lie down with him — his intent was to bind him by intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Finding that Daxingguo had no treasonous intent of his own, he summoned him to his bedchamber, ordered him to undress, and tried to share his bed — seeking to bind him by intimacy.

sentences.zh: 興國固辭不敢，曰：「即有使，惟大王之命。」

translations.literal: Daxingguo firmly declined and dared not comply, saying: "If there is any commission, it is only at the Great King's command.
translations.idiomatic: Daxingguo firmly refused. He said: "If you have a commission for me, I await only the Great King's command.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「主上無故殺常勝，又殺皇后。

translations.literal: 」Hailing said: "The sovereign for no reason killed Changsheng and also killed the empress.
translations.idiomatic: 」Hailing said: "The sovereign murdered Changsheng for no reason — and murdered the empress as well.

sentences.zh: 乃以常勝家產賜阿楞，既又殺阿楞，遂以賜我。

translations.literal: Then he gave Changsheng's family property to Aleng; after that he killed Aleng as well, and then gave it to me.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Changsheng's estate to Aleng, then killed Aleng too — and gave it to me.

sentences.zh: 我深以為憂，奈何？」

translations.literal: I am deeply troubled by this — what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: I am deeply troubled — what can be done?

sentences.zh: 興國曰：「是固可慮也。」

translations.literal: 」Daxingguo said: "That is indeed a matter for concern.
translations.idiomatic: 」Daxingguo said: "That is indeed worrisome.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「朝臣旦夕危懼，皆不自保。

translations.literal: 」Hailing said: "The court ministers live in daily fear and cannot even preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: 」Hailing said: "The ministers live in daily fear — none can feel safe.

sentences.zh: 向者我生日，因皇后附賜物，君遂被杖，我亦見疑。

translations.literal: Earlier, on my birthday, because the empress attached gifts to the presentation, you were beaten with the staff, and I too came under suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: On my birthday, because the empress added her gifts, you were beaten — and I fell under suspicion too.

sentences.zh: 主上嘗言會須殺君，我與君皆將不免，寧坐待死何如舉大事。

translations.literal: The sovereign once said he would have to kill you; both you and I will not escape — is it better to sit and await death, or to undertake a great affair?
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign once said he would have to kill you. Neither of us will be spared — better to raise a coup than sit and await death.

sentences.zh: 我與大臣數人謀議已定，爾以為如何？」

translations.literal: I and several great ministers have already settled our deliberations — what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Several ministers and I have already agreed on a plan — what do you say?

sentences.zh: 興國曰：「如大王言，事不可緩也。」

translations.literal: 」Xingguo said: "As the Great King says, the matter cannot be delayed."
translations.idiomatic: 」Xingguo said: "As you say, Great King — this cannot wait."

sentences.zh: 乃約十二月九日夜起事。

translations.literal: 」They then set the night of the ninth day of the twelfth month to launch the affair.
translations.idiomatic: 」They fixed the night of the ninth of the twelfth month to strike.

sentences.zh: 興國取符鑰開門，矯詔召海陵入。

translations.literal: Xingguo took the tally and keys, opened the gate, and by forged edict summoned Hailing to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Xingguo seized the palace tally and keys, opened the gate, and forged an edict summoning Hailing inside.

sentences.zh: 夜二更，海陵、秉德等入。

translations.literal: At the second watch of the night, Hailing, Bingde, and the others entered.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch, Hailing, Bingde, and the rest entered.

sentences.zh: 熙宗常置佩刀於禦榻上，是夜興國先取投榻下，及亂作，熙宗求佩刀不得，遂遇弑。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong usually kept his girdle knife on the imperial couch; that night Xingguo first took it and threw it under the couch, and when the disturbance broke out Emperor Xizong sought his girdle knife but could not find it, and so met assassination.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong usually kept his sword on the imperial couch. That night Xingguo removed it and tossed it under the bed. When the attack began, Xizong groped for his blade and found nothing — and was murdered.

sentences.zh: 海陵既立，以興國為廣甯尹，賜奴婢百口、犀玉帶各一、錢絹馬牛鐵券如其黨，進階金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Once Hailing was enthroned, he appointed Xingguo metropolitan guardian of Guangning, granted a hundred male and female servants, one rhinoceros-horn belt and one jade belt each, cash, silk, horses, oxen, and an iron certificate like his fellow conspirators, and promoted him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing took the throne, he made Xingguo guardian of Guangning, rewarded him with a hundred servants, rhinoceros and jade belts, cash, silk, horses, oxen, and an iron certificate like the other conspirators, and promoted him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 再賜興國錢千萬、黃金四百兩、銀千兩、良馬四匹、駝車一乘、橐駝三頭、真珠巾、玉鉤帶、玉佩刀、及玉校鞍轡。

translations.literal: He further rewarded Xingguo with ten million in cash, four hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, four fine horses, one camel carriage, three baggage camels, a pearl headcloth, a jade hook belt, a jade girdle knife, and jade-trimmed saddle and bridle.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Xingguo another ten million cash, four hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, four fine horses, a camel carriage, three pack camels, a pearl headcloth, jade hook belt, jade sword, and jade-trimmed saddle and bridle.

sentences.zh: 天德四年，改崇義軍節度使，賜名邦基。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiande, he was transferred to military commissioner of the Chongyi Army and granted the name Bangji.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 4 he became military commissioner of the Chongyi Army and was granted the name Bangji.

sentences.zh: 再授絳陽、武甯節度使，改河間尹。

translations.literal: He was again appointed military commissioner of Jiangyang and Wuning, then transferred to metropolitan guardian of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made military commissioner of Jiangyang and Wuning, then transferred to guardian of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，廢於家，凡海陵所賜皆奪之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Bangji was dismissed and kept at home; everything Hailing had granted him was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Bangji was stripped of office and confined at home; every gift from Hailing was seized back.

sentences.zh: 大定中，邦基兄邦傑自京兆判官還，世宗曰：「大邦傑因其弟進，濫廁縉紳，豈可復用。」

translations.literal: During the Dading era, Bangji's elder brother Bangjie returned from serving as aide to the prefect of Jingzhao; Emperor Shizong said: "Great Bangjie advanced through his younger brother's connection and was improperly seated among the gentry — how can he be employed again?"
translations.idiomatic: During Dading, Bangji's elder brother Bangjie returned from a post as Jingzhao prefectural aide. Emperor Shizong said: "Bangjie rose only through his brother and never deserved a place among the gentry — he must not serve again."

sentences.zh: 並罷其子弟與所贈父官。

translations.literal: 」Their sons and younger brothers were dismissed together, and the offices granted to their father were revoked.
translations.idiomatic: 」Their sons and brothers were all dismissed, and the offices granted their father were revoked.

sentences.zh: 及海陵降為庶人，詔曰：「大邦基與海陵同謀弑逆，逋誅至今，為幸多矣。」

translations.literal: When Hailing was demoted to commoner status, an edict said: "Great Bangji plotted regicide together with Hailing; to have escaped execution until now was already great fortune."
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing was reduced to commoner rank, an edict declared: "Bangji conspired with Hailing in regicide — to have escaped death this long was fortune enough."

sentences.zh: 遂磔於思陵之側。

translations.literal: 」He was then dismembered by slicing beside Siling.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was dismembered beside Siling.

sentences.zh: 徒單阿里出虎

translations.literal: Tudan Aluchuhu
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Aluchuhu

sentences.zh: 徒單阿里出虎，會甯葛馬合窟申人，徙懿州。

translations.literal: Tudan Aluchuhu, a man of Gemahekuishen in Huining, was relocated to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Aluchuhu, from Gemahekuishen in Huining, was resettled at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 父拔改，太祖時有戰功，領謀克，曷速館軍帥，皇統四年為兵部侍郎，歷天德軍節度使，改興中尹，與宗幹世為姻家。

translations.literal: His father Bage had military merit under Emperor Taizu, held a company captaincy, and was army commander of Yisuguan; in the fourth year of Huangtong he became vice minister of war, served as military commissioner of the Tiande Army, was transferred to metropolitan guardian of Xingzhong, and was for generations affined with Prince of Liao Zonggan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bage won distinction under Emperor Taizu, served as company captain and commander of the Yisuguan army, became vice minister of war in Huangtong 4, held the Tiande Army command, then became guardian of Xingzhong — his family and Prince of Liao Zonggan's had been intermarried for generations.

sentences.zh: 皇統九年，阿里出虎與僕散忽土俱為護衛十人長。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Huangtong, Aluchuhu and Pusan Hu Tu both served as captains of the ten-man palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 9, Aluchuhu and Hu Tu both commanded units in the ten-man palace guard.

sentences.zh: 海陵將弑熙宗，欲得二人者為內應，遂許以女妻阿里出虎子，而以逆謀告之。

translations.literal: When Hailing was about to assassinate Emperor Xizong, he wished to have the two as inside collaborators; he therefore promised to give his daughter in marriage to Aluchuhu's son and disclosed the treasonous plot to them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing plotted to murder Emperor Xizong, he wanted the two as inside men — he promised his daughter to Aluchuhu's son and revealed the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 阿里出虎素凶暴，聞其言喜甚，曰：「阿家此言何晚邪，廢立之事亦男子所為。

translations.literal: Aluchuhu was by nature fierce and violent; hearing these words he was greatly pleased and said: "Uncle, why speak so late? Deposing and enthroning is also what a man should do.
translations.idiomatic: Aluchuhu was a brutal man. He was delighted and said: "Uncle, why wait so long? Overthrowing an emperor is men's work.

sentences.zh: 主上不能保天下，人望所屬惟在阿家，今日之謀乃我素志也。」

translations.literal: The sovereign cannot preserve the realm; men's hopes rest on Uncle alone — today's plot has long been my own wish."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cannot hold the realm; all eyes are on you, Uncle — this plot is exactly what I have wanted."

sentences.zh: 遂與忽土俱以十二月九日直禁中，海陵故以是夜二更入宮，至寢殿，阿里出虎先進刃，忽土次之，熙宗頓僕，海陵復刃之，血濺其面及衣。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon he and Hu Tu both served inside the palace on the ninth day of the twelfth month; Hailing therefore entered the palace at the second watch that night, and reaching the sleeping hall, Aluchuhu struck first with the blade, Hu Tu next; Emperor Xizong collapsed, Hailing stabbed him again, and blood splashed on his face and clothes.
translations.idiomatic: 」He and Hu Tu drew palace duty on the ninth of the twelfth month. Hailing entered at the second watch that night. In the sleeping hall Aluchuhu struck first, Hu Tu second; Emperor Xizong fell, Hailing stabbed him again, and blood spattered Hailing's face and robes.

sentences.zh: 海陵既立，以阿里出虎為右副點檢，賜錢絹馬牛羊如其黨，子術斯剌尚榮國公主合女，加昭毅大將軍駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Once Hailing was enthroned, he appointed Aluchuhu right vice chief inspector, granted cash, silk, horses, oxen, and sheep like his fellow conspirators, and had his son Shusila marry Princess Rongguo Heyue and promoted him to General of Manifest Valor and chief consort commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing took the throne, he made Aluchuhu right vice chief inspector and rewarded him like the other conspirators; his son Shusila married Princess Rongguo Heyue and was made General of Manifest Valor and chief consort commander.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，留守東京，加儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he remained as guardian of Dongjing and was given honorary Three Excellencies rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 2 he stayed on as guardian of Dongjing and received honorary Three Excellencies rank.

sentences.zh: 八月，改河間尹，世襲臨潢府路斜剌阿猛安領親管謀克。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was transferred to metropolitan guardian of Hejian and inherited the office of commander of the Xielia militia in the Linhuang Circuit, personally commanding a company captaincy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he became guardian of Hejian and inherited command of the Xielia militia in Linhuang Circuit with personal company captaincy.

sentences.zh: 以憂去職，起復為太原尹，封王。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning leave, was recalled from mourning to serve as metropolitan guardian of Taiyuan, and was enfeoffed as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to mourn, was recalled as guardian of Taiyuan, and was enfeoffed as a prince.

sentences.zh: 阿里出虎自謂有佐立功，受鐵券，凶狠益甚，奴視僚屬，少忤其意輒箠辱無所恤。

translations.literal: Aluchuhu considered himself to have merit in assisting enthronement, held an iron certificate, and grew ever more cruel; he treated subordinates like slaves, and whoever slightly crossed his will he at once beat and humiliated without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Aluchuhu counted his enthronement service a great deed and grew ever crueler with his iron certificate in hand. He treated subordinates like slaves and beat anyone who crossed him.

sentences.zh: 嘗問休咎于卜者高鼎，遂以鼎所占問張王乞。

translations.literal: He once asked the diviner Gao Ding about good and ill fortune, then had Zhang Wangqi questioned about what Ding had divined.
translations.idiomatic: He once asked the diviner Gao Ding about his fortune, then questioned Zhang Wangqi about Ding's reading.

sentences.zh: 王乞以謂當有天命，阿里出虎喜，以王乞語告鼎。

translations.literal: Wangqi said he believed there would be a mandate of Heaven; Aluchuhu was pleased and told Ding what Wangqi had said.
translations.idiomatic: Wangqi declared that Heaven's mandate was at hand. Aluchuhu was delighted and told Ding what Wangqi had said.

sentences.zh: 鼎上變，阿里出虎伏誅，並殺其妻及王乞。

translations.literal: Ding reported the matter to the throne; Aluchuhu accepted execution, and his wife and Wangqi were killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Ding reported the treason. Aluchuhu was executed, along with his wife and Wangqi.

sentences.zh: 海陵使其子術斯剌焚其屍，投骨水中。

translations.literal: Hailing had his son Shusila burn the corpse and cast the bones into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had Shusila burn the body and throw the bones into the river.

sentences.zh: 拔改自西京留守曆西南路招討使、忠順軍節度使，入為勸農使，復為河間尹，改臨洮尹，入為工部尚書，改興平軍節度使，濟南尹，卒。

translations.literal: Bage, from guardian of the Western Capital, served as pacification commissioner of the Southwest Circuit and military commissioner of the Zhongshun Army, entered the capital as promotion-of-agriculture commissioner, again served as metropolitan guardian of Hejian, was transferred to metropolitan guardian of Lintao, entered the capital as minister of works, was transferred to military commissioner of the Xingping Army and metropolitan guardian of Jinan, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Bage rose from guardian of the Western Capital through pacification commissioner of the Southwest Circuit and Zhongshun Army command, then promotion-of-agriculture commissioner, guardian of Hejian, guardian of Lintao, minister of works, Xingping Army commissioner and guardian of Jinan, where he died.

sentences.zh: 僕散師恭

translations.literal: Pusan Shigong
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Shigong

sentences.zh: 僕散師恭，本名忽土，上京老海達葛人。

translations.literal: Pusan Shigong, original name Hu Tu, was a man of Lao Haidage in Shangjing.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Shigong, born Hu Tu, came from Lao Haidage in Shangjing.

sentences.zh: 本微賤，宗幹嘗周恤之，擢置宿衛為十人長。

translations.literal: He was originally of humble status; Prince of Liao Zonggan once looked after and comforted him, raised him to palace guard service, and made him a captain of the ten-man guard.
translations.idiomatic: Born low, he was taken in by Prince of Liao Zonggan, brought into the palace guard, and made a ten-man captain.

sentences.zh: 海陵謀逆，以忽土出自其家，有恩，欲使為內應，謂之曰：「我有一言欲告君久矣，恐泄於人，未敢也。」

translations.literal: When Hailing plotted rebellion, because Hu Tu came from his household and owed a debt of gratitude, he wished to make him an inside collaborator and said to him: "I have long wanted to tell you something, but feared it would leak to others and dared not."
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing plotted treason, he meant to use Hu Tu — a man from Zonggan's household who owed him — as an inside man. He said: "I have long wanted to tell you something, but feared it would leak."

sentences.zh: 忽土曰：「肌肉之外，皆先太師所賜，苟有補于國王，死不敢辭。」

translations.literal: 」Hu Tu said: "Except for my flesh, all I have was granted by the late Grand Preceptor; if it can serve the state's king, I dare not refuse even death."
translations.idiomatic: 」Hu Tu said: "Everything I have beyond my own flesh came from the late Grand Preceptor — if it serves the king and state, I will not shrink from death."

sentences.zh: 先太師，謂宗幹也。

translations.literal: 」"The late Grand Preceptor" meant Prince of Liao Zonggan.
translations.idiomatic: 」The "late Grand Preceptor" was Prince of Liao Zonggan.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「主上失道，吾將行廢立事，必得君為助乃可。」

translations.literal: Hailing said: "The sovereign has lost the Way; I intend to carry out deposition and enthronement — I must have your help."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said: "The emperor has lost the Way. I mean to depose him and set up another — I need your help."

sentences.zh: 忽土許之。

translations.literal: 」Hu Tu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: 」Hu Tu agreed.

sentences.zh: 十二月九日，忽土直宿，海陵因之入宮。

translations.literal: On the ninth day of the twelfth month Hu Tu was on night duty, and Hailing entered the palace by this means.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth of the twelfth month Hu Tu stood night watch, and Hailing used that opening to enter the palace.

sentences.zh: 至寢殿，熙宗聞步屣聲，咄之，眾皆卻立不敢動，忽土曰：「事至此，不進得乎？」

translations.literal: Reaching the sleeping hall, Emperor Xizong heard the sound of shuffling steps and shouted at them; all stepped back and dared not move; Hu Tu said: "The affair has come to this — can we not advance?"
translations.idiomatic: At the sleeping hall Emperor Xizong heard footsteps and shouted. The others froze. Hu Tu said: "We have come this far — can we turn back?"

sentences.zh: 乃相與排闥而入。

translations.literal: 」Then together they pushed open the door and entered.
translations.idiomatic: 」Together they burst through the door.

sentences.zh: 既弑熙宗，秉德等尚未有所屬，忽土曰：「始者議立平章，今復何疑。」

translations.literal: After Emperor Xizong was assassinated, Bingde and the others still had no one to follow; Hu Tu said: "At the start we agreed to enthrone the Chief Councillor — what doubt remains now?"
translations.idiomatic: After the murder Bingde and the rest still had no candidate. Hu Tu said: "We agreed from the start to make the Chief Councillor emperor — why hesitate now?"

sentences.zh: 乃奉海陵坐，眾前稱萬歲。

translations.literal: 」They then seated Hailing, and all before him cried ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: 」They seated Hailing on the throne and cried "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 遂召曹國王宗敏至，即使忽土殺之。

translations.literal: They then summoned Prince of Cao Zongmin and at once had Hu Tu kill him.
translations.idiomatic: They summoned Prince of Cao Zongmin and had Hu Tu kill him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 既即位，忽土為左副點檢，賜錢絹馬牛羊鐵券。

translations.literal: Once enthroned, Hu Tu was made left vice chief inspector and granted cash, silk, horses, oxen, sheep, and an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: After enthronement Hu Tu became left vice chief inspector and received cash, silk, horses, oxen, sheep, and an iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 轉都點檢，改名師恭。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief inspector and renamed Shigong.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief inspector and was renamed Shigong.

sentences.zh: 遷會甯牧，拜太子少師、工部尚書，封王。

translations.literal: He was transferred to pasture director of Huining, appointed junior preceptor to the crown prince and minister of works, and enfeoffed as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: He became pasture director of Huining, junior preceptor to the crown prince, minister of works, and a prince.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以憂解職。

translations.literal: Before long he left office on mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he resigned to mourn.

sentences.zh: 起復為樞密副使，進拜樞密使。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning, he became vice privy councilor and was promoted to privy councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he became vice privy councilor, then privy councilor.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，為右丞相。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan he became right chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 3 he became right chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 正隆初，拜太尉，復為樞密使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenglong he was appointed grand commandant and again served as privy councilor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhenglong he was made grand commandant and again privy councilor.

sentences.zh: 無何，以憂去，起復為太尉、樞密使。

translations.literal: Before long he left on mourning leave, was recalled from mourning, and again served as grand commandant and privy councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left to mourn again, was recalled, and again held the posts of grand commandant and privy councilor.

sentences.zh: 海陵至汴京，賜忽土第一區，鄰甯德宮。

translations.literal: When Hailing arrived at Bianjing, he granted Hu Tu one grand residence adjacent to Bingde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing reached Bianjing he gave Hu Tu a grand mansion next to Bingde Palace.

sentences.zh: 宮，徒單太后所居也，忽土時時入見太后。

translations.literal: The palace was where Empress Dowager Tudan resided; Hu Tu from time to time entered to see the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Tudan lived in that palace, and Hu Tu visited her often.

sentences.zh: 及契丹撒八反，海陵命忽土與蕭懷忠北伐。

translations.literal: When the Khitan Saba rebelled, Hailing ordered Hu Tu and Xiao Huaizhong to campaign north.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan rebel Saba rose, Hailing sent Hu Tu and Xiao Huaizhong north.

sentences.zh: 比行，忽土入辭甯德，太后與語久之。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure Hu Tu went to take leave at Bingde Palace; the empress dowager spoke with him for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Before marching, Hu Tu took leave at Bingde Palace and talked with the empress dowager at length.

sentences.zh: 海陵聞而惡之，疑其與太后有異謀。

translations.literal: Hailing heard of this and resented it, suspecting that he and the empress dowager had some other plot.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing heard of it and grew suspicious — he feared Hu Tu and the empress dowager were plotting together.

sentences.zh: 是時，蕭禿剌、斡盧補與契丹撒八連戰皆無功，糧運不繼，乃退軍臨潢。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Tula, Wolubu, and the Khitan Saba fought repeatedly without success; grain transport could not keep up, and the army retreated to Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tula and Wolubu fought Saba repeatedly without success. Supplies failed, and the army fell back to Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 而撒八聞師恭以大軍且至，乃謀歸大石，沿龍駒河西去。

translations.literal: When Saba heard that Shigong was coming with a great army, he planned to submit to Dashi and withdrew west along the Longju River.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Shigong was advancing with a large force, Saba meant to join Dashi and withdrew west along the Longju River.

sentences.zh: 師恭至臨潢，追之不及。

translations.literal: Shigong reached Linhuang but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Shigong reached Linhuang but could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 海陵使樞密副使白彥敬等討撒八，師恭還，遣其子忽殺虎乘傳逆之，至則執而戮於市。

translations.literal: Hailing sent Vice Privy Councilor Bai Yanjing and others to attack Saba; Shigong returned, and Hailing dispatched his son Husha Hu by fast relay to intercept him — when he arrived Shigong was seized and executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing sent Vice Privy Councilor Bai Yanjing after Saba. Shigong was heading home when Hailing's son Husha Hu rode ahead by relay post, seized him, and had him executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 師恭臨刑，繩枚窒口不能言，但舉首視天日而已。

translations.literal: At execution Shigong's mouth was stopped with rope and a gag and he could not speak; he only raised his head and looked toward the sun.
translations.idiomatic: At the block Shigong's mouth was gagged — he could not speak, only lift his head to the sky.

sentences.zh: 遂族滅之，並誅滅蕭禿剌、蕭賾、蕭懷忠家。

translations.literal: His clan was then exterminated, and the families of Xiao Tula, Xiao Ze, and Xiao Huaizhong were also destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: His entire clan was wiped out, along with the families of Xiao Tula, Xiao Ze, and Xiao Huaizhong.

sentences.zh: 大定初，皆復官爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading, all their offices and titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading their offices and titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 及海陵降為庶人，師恭以預弑復削之。

translations.literal: When Hailing was demoted to commoner status, Shigong's restorations were again stripped because he had taken part in the assassination.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing was reduced to commoner rank, Shigong's honors were stripped again for his part in the regicide.

sentences.zh: 世宗幸上京，過老海達葛。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong visited Shangjing, he passed through Lao Haidage.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong visited Shangjing, he passed through Lao Haidage.

sentences.zh: 師恭族人臨潢尹守中、定遠大將軍阿里徒等皆奪官。

translations.literal: Shigong's clansmen Linhuang guardian Shouzhong, General of Dingyuan Ali Tu, and others all had their offices removed.
translations.idiomatic: Shigong's kinsmen — Linhuang guardian Shouzhong, General of Dingyuan Ali Tu, and others — were all stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上謂宰相曰；

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the emperor said to the chief councilors:
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year the emperor told his chief councilors:

sentences.zh: 「海陵遣僕散師恭、蕭禿剌、蕭懷忠追撒八不及，皆坐誅，遂夷其族，虐之甚也。」

translations.literal: "Hailing sent Pusan Shigong, Xiao Tula, and Xiao Huaizhong to pursue Saba but they could not overtake him; all were condemned and executed, and their clans were exterminated — the cruelty was extreme."
translations.idiomatic: "Hailing sent Pusan Shigong, Xiao Tula, and Xiao Huaizhong after Saba. They failed to catch him, yet all were executed and their clans wiped out — that was brutal in the extreme."

sentences.zh: 平章政事襄對曰：「是時臣在軍中，忽土、賾有精甲一萬三千有餘，賊軍雖多皆脅從之人，以氈紙為甲，易與也。

translations.literal: 」Chief Councilor Xiang replied: "At that time your servant was in the army. Hu Tu and Ze had more than thirteen thousand men in fine armor; though the rebel force was large, they were all coerced followers with felt and paper for armor — easy to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: 」Chief Councilor Xiang replied: "I was in the field then. Hu Tu and Ze had over thirteen thousand well-armed men. Saba's force was mostly coerced followers in felt and paper armor — they would have been easy to defeat.

sentences.zh: 忽土等恇怯遷延，賊乃遁去。」

translations.literal: Hu Tu and the others were cowardly and delayed, and the rebels escaped."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Tu and the others hung back in cowardice, and the rebels got away."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「審如是，則誅之可也。」

translations.literal: 」The emperor said: "If it was truly so, then executing them would have been permissible."
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor said: "If that is so, then execution was justified."

sentences.zh: 兄渾坦。

translations.literal: 」His elder brother was Huntan.
translations.idiomatic: 」His elder brother was Huntan.

sentences.zh: 徒單貞

translations.literal: Tudan Zhen
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Zhen

sentences.zh: 徒單貞，本名特思，忒黑辟剌人也。

translations.literal: Tudan Zhen, original name Tesi, was a man of Teihepila.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Zhen, born Tesi, came from Teihepila.

sentences.zh: 祖抄，從太祖伐遼有功，授世襲猛安。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chao had merit following Emperor Taizu in campaigning against Liao and was granted an hereditary commandery command.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chao won distinction campaigning against Liao under Emperor Taizu and received an hereditary commandery command.

sentences.zh: 父婆盧火，以戰功累官開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His father Poluhuo, through military merit, rose in office to Right with Three Excellencies Rank Opening the Mansion.
translations.idiomatic: His father Poluhuo rose through battlefield service to Right with Three Excellencies Rank Opening the Mansion.

sentences.zh: 貞娶遼王宗幹女，海陵同母女弟也。

translations.literal: Zhen married a daughter of Prince of Liao Zonggan, a younger sister by the same mother as Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen married a daughter of Prince of Liao Zonggan — Hailing's younger uterine sister.

sentences.zh: 皇統九年、貞與海陵俱弑熙宗。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Huangtong, Zhen and Hailing together assassinated Emperor Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 9, Zhen and Hailing together murdered Emperor Xizong.

sentences.zh: 海陵既立，以貞為左衛將軍，封貞妻平陽長公主，貞為駙馬都尉、殿前左副點檢。

translations.literal: Once Hailing was enthroned, he appointed Zhen left guard general, enfeoffed Zhen's wife as Princess Chang of Pingyang, and made Zhen chief consort commander and left vice chief inspector before the palace.
translations.idiomatic: After enthronement Hailing made Zhen left guard general, enfeoffed his wife as Princess Chang of Pingyang, and appointed Zhen chief consort commander and left vice chief inspector before the palace.

sentences.zh: 轉都點檢，兼太子少保，封王。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief inspector, concurrently junior guardian to the crown prince, and enfeoffed as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief inspector and junior guardian to the crown prince and was enfeoffed as a prince.

sentences.zh: 改大興尹，都點檢如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to metropolitan guardian of Daxing while retaining the chief inspectorship.
translations.idiomatic: He became guardian of Daxing while keeping the chief inspectorship.

sentences.zh: 俄授臨潢府路昏斯魯猛安。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed commander of the Hunslu militia in the Linhuang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made commander of the Hunslu militia in Linhuang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 居二年，海陵召貞勖之曰：「汝自幼常在左右，頗著微勞，而近日乃怠忽，縱有罪，樹私恩。

translations.literal: After two years Hailing summoned Zhen and admonished him, saying: "From youth you have always been at my side and have done some small service, yet recently you have grown negligent; even if guilty of offense, you show favoritism in private.
translations.idiomatic: After two years Hailing summoned Zhen and warned him: "You have been at my side since youth and done good service, yet lately you have grown slack — even when men deserve punishment, you show them private favor.

sentences.zh: 凡人富貴而驕，皆死征也。

translations.literal: Whenever anyone grows rich and honored yet arrogant, that is a sign of death.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and rank breed arrogance — and arrogance is a death warrant.

sentences.zh: 汝若不制汝心，將無所不至，賜之死復何辭。

translations.literal: If you do not restrain your heart, there will be nothing you will not do; were I to grant you death, what would you have to say?
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot govern yourself, there is no limit to what you will do — and if I put you to death, what excuse would you have?

sentences.zh: 朕念弟襄及公主與朕同胞，故少示懲戒。」

translations.literal: I think of my brother Xiang and the princess, who share my womb — therefore I show you a lesser punishment as warning."
translations.idiomatic: I spare you only because my brother Xiang and the princess are my full siblings — consider this a warning."

sentences.zh: 貞但號泣。

translations.literal: 」Zhen only wailed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: 」Zhen could only weep.

sentences.zh: 即日解點檢職，仍為大興尹，復戒之曰：「今而後能以勤自勵，朕當思之。

translations.literal: That same day he was removed from the chief inspectorship but remained metropolitan guardian of Daxing; Hailing again warned him: "From now on, if you can spur yourself to diligence, I will bear it in mind.
translations.idiomatic: That day he lost the chief inspectorship but kept the guardianship of Daxing. Hailing warned him again: "If you exert yourself hereafter, I will remember it.

sentences.zh: 不然，黜爾歸田里矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise I will dismiss you and send you back to the fields."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I will strip you of office and send you home to the fields."

sentences.zh: 逾月，復為都點檢、大興尹如故。

translations.literal: 」After a month he again held the chief inspectorship and metropolitan guardianship of Daxing as before.
translations.idiomatic: 」Within a month he was restored as chief inspector and guardian of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，例封沈。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shen under the standard practice.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 2 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shen.

sentences.zh: 遷樞密副使，賜佩刀入宮，轉同判大宗正事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice privy councilor, granted a girdle knife for entry to the palace, and transferred to associate director of the Imperial Clan Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice privy councilor, was granted a palace sword, and was made associate director of the Imperial Clan Bureau.

sentences.zh: 海陵將伐宋，詔朝官除三國人使宴飲，其餘飲酒者死。

translations.literal: When Hailing was about to attack Song, he decreed that among court officials only envoys from the three states might feast and drink; any others who drank would die.
translations.idiomatic: As Hailing prepared to attack Song, he decreed that only envoys from the three states might drink at court — anyone else who drank would die.

sentences.zh: 六年正月四日立春節，益都尹京、安武節度使爽、金吾上將軍阿速飲於貞第。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the first month of the sixth year, the Beginning-of-Spring festival, Yidu guardian Jing, Anwu military commissioner Shuang, and Gold Guard senior general Asu drank at Zhen's residence.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth of the first month in the sixth year — Beginning-of-Spring day — Yidu guardian Jing, Anwu commissioner Shuang, and Gold Guard general Asu drank at Zhen's house.

sentences.zh: 海陵使周福兒賜土牛至貞第，見之以告，海陵召貞詰之曰：「戎事方殷，禁百官飲酒，卿等知之乎？」

translations.literal: Hailing sent Zhou Fu'er to present the clay ox at Zhen's residence; seeing them he reported it, and Hailing summoned Zhen and interrogated him: "Military affairs are pressing and drinking is forbidden to all officials — were you aware?"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing sent Zhou Fu'er with the ceremonial clay ox to Zhen's house. Zhou saw them drinking and reported it. Hailing summoned Zhen and demanded: "War is imminent and drinking is forbidden — did you know?"

sentences.zh: 貞等伏地請死，海陵數之曰：「汝等若以飲酒殺人太重，固當諫，古人三諫不聽亦勉從君命。

translations.literal: 」Zhen and the others prostrated themselves and asked for death; Hailing reproached them: "If you thought death for drinking too harsh, you should have remonstrated — ancients remonstrated thrice, and if not heeded still strove to obey the sovereign's command.
translations.idiomatic: 」Zhen and the others prostrated themselves and begged for death. Hailing rebuked them: "If you thought the penalty too harsh, you should have remonstrated — the ancients advised three times, and even when ignored still obeyed their ruler.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝《軍行令》曰'犯麥者死'。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei's "Army March Order" says: "Whoever tramples the wheat shall die."
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Wu of Wei wrote in his Army March Order: "Whoever tramples the wheat dies."

sentences.zh: 已而所乘馬入麥中，乃割發以自刑。

translations.literal: Before long the horse he was riding entered among the wheat, and thereupon he cut off his hair to punish himself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his horse trampled the wheat, and he punished himself by cutting off his hair.

sentences.zh: 犯麥，微事也，然必欲以示信。

translations.literal: Trampling wheat is a small matter, yet he insisted on demonstrating good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Trampling wheat was a petty offense, yet he was determined to prove his word.

sentences.zh: 朕為天下主，法不能行於貴近乎？

translations.literal: I am lord of all under Heaven — can the law not be enforced on those close and dear to me?
translations.idiomatic: I rule all under Heaven — shall the law fail to reach those nearest me?

sentences.zh: 朕念慈憲太后子四人，惟朕與公主在，而京等皆近屬，曲貸死罪。」

translations.literal: I reflect that Empress Dowager Cixian had four sons; only I and the princess remain, and Jing and the others are all close kin — I leniently spare them the death penalty."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Cixian had four sons; only the princess and I survive. Jing and the others are close relatives — I mercifully commute the death sentence."

sentences.zh: 於是杖貞七十，京等三人各杖一百，降貞為安武軍節度使，京為灤州刺史，爽歸化州刺史。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon Zhen was beaten seventy strokes with the staff; Jing and the other three each a hundred strokes. Zhen was demoted to military commissioner of the Anwu Army, Jing to prefect of Luanzhou, and Shuang to prefect of Guihua.
translations.idiomatic: 」Zhen received seventy strokes; Jing and the other three a hundred each. Zhen was demoted to Anwu commissioner, Jing became prefect of Luan, and Shuang prefect of Guihua.

sentences.zh: 無何，拜貞御史大夫，以本官為左監軍，從伐宋。

translations.literal: Before long Zhen was appointed Censor-in-Chief; with his existing office he served as left army supervisor and joined the campaign against Song.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhen was made censor-in-chief and left army supervisor and marched against Song.

sentences.zh: 至揚州，海陵死，北還。

translations.literal: When they reached Yangzhou, Hailing died, and they returned north.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangzhou Hailing was killed, and the army turned north.

sentences.zh: 見世宗於中都，詔以貞女為皇太子妃，除貞為太原尹，改咸平。

translations.literal: He had audience with Emperor Shizong at the Central Capital; an edict made Zhen's daughter crown princess, appointed Zhen metropolitan guardian of Taiyuan, and transferred him to Xianping.
translations.idiomatic: He had audience with Shizong at the Central Capital. The emperor made Zhen's daughter crown princess, appointed Zhen guardian of Taiyuan, then transferred him to Xianping.

sentences.zh: 貞在咸平貪污不法，累贓巨萬，徙真定尹，事覺。

translations.literal: At Xianping Zhen was corrupt and lawless, amassing ill-gotten gains in the tens of thousands; he was transferred to be metropolitan guardian of Zhending, and the matter came to light.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianping Zhen grew corrupt, amassing vast bribes. He was moved to Zhending, where the scandal broke.

sentences.zh: 世宗使大理卿李昌圖鞫之，貞即引伏，昌圖還奏，上問之曰：「貞停職否？」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong sent Court of Judicial Review director Li Changtu to investigate; Zhen at once confessed, and when Changtu returned to report, the emperor asked: "Has Zhen been suspended from office?"
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent judicial review director Li Changtu to investigate. Zhen confessed at once. When Changtu reported back, the emperor asked: "Has Zhen been suspended?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「未也。」

translations.literal: 」He replied: "Not yet."
translations.idiomatic: 」"Not yet," he replied.

sentences.zh: 上怒，抵昌圖罪，復遣刑部尚書移剌道往真定問之，征其贓還主。

translations.literal: 」The emperor was angry, penalized Changtu for his offense, and again sent Minister of Punishments Yelü Dao to Zhending to investigate, seizing the stolen goods to return them to their owners.
translations.idiomatic: 」Enraged, the emperor punished Changtu and sent Minister of Punishments Yelü Dao to Zhending to pursue the case and recover the plunder for its owners.

sentences.zh: 有司征給不以時，詔先以官錢還其主，而令貞納官。

translations.literal: When the authorities failed to collect and disburse in timely fashion, an edict ordered that owners first be repaid from official funds, while Zhen was to reimburse the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Because recovery lagged, the court ordered victims repaid from public funds first, with Zhen to make restitution to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 凡還主髒，皆准此例。

translations.literal: All cases of returning stolen goods to owners were made to follow this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all restitution to victims followed this rule.

sentences.zh: 降貞為博州防禦使，降貞妻為清平縣主。

translations.literal: Zhen was demoted to defense commissioner of Bozhou, and Zhen's wife was demoted to county mistress of Qingping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was demoted to defense commissioner of Bozhou; his wife was stripped to county mistress of Qingping.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷震武節度使，遣使者往戒敕之，詔曰：「朕念卿懿戚，不待終考，更遷大鎮。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to military commissioner of Zhenwu; an envoy was sent to admonish him, and the edict said: "Mindful that you are my kinsman by marriage, I have not waited for your term to end before transferring you to a great command.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made commissioner of Zhenwu, with an envoy sent to warn him: "As my kinsman by marriage, you are promoted to a major command before your term has ended.

sentences.zh: 非常之恩不可數得，卿勿蹈前過。」

translations.literal: Extraordinary favor cannot be gained repeatedly — do not repeat your former faults."
translations.idiomatic: Such extraordinary grace cannot come twice — do not repeat your past mistakes."

sentences.zh: 轉河中尹。

translations.literal: 」He was transferred to metropolitan guardian of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was transferred to guardian of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 進封其妻為任國公主，賜黃金百兩、重彩二十端，賜貞擊球馬二匹。

translations.literal: His wife was advanced in rank to Princess of Renguo; there were granted a hundred taels of gold and twenty bolts of heavy brocade, and Zhen was given two polo ponies.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was ennobled Princess of Renguo and given a hundred taels of gold and twenty bolts of brocade; Zhen received two polo horses.

sentences.zh: 改東京留守，賜玉吐鶻、弓矢，賜貞妻錢萬貫。

translations.literal: He was made guardian of the Eastern Capital; jade gyrfalcon ornaments and bow and arrows were granted, and Zhen's wife was given ten thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: He became guardian of the Eastern Capital, was granted jade gyrfalcon fittings and bow and arrows, and his wife received ten thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「海陵已貶為庶人，宗幹不當猶稱帝。」

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "Hailing has already been degraded to commoner status — Prince of Liao Zonggan ought not still to be styled emperor."
translations.idiomatic: The ministries reported: "Hailing has been demoted to commoner rank — Prince of Liao Zonggan should no longer be addressed as emperor."

sentences.zh: 於是，以宗幹有社稷功，詔追封為遼主，其子孫及諸女皆降，貞妻降永平縣主，貞自儀同三司降特進，奪猛安，不稱駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon, because Zonggan had merit for the state, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Liao; his descendants and all his daughters were demoted — Zhen's wife to county mistress of Yongping, Zhen from Director with Threefold Parity to Special Grand Master; his meng'an was revoked and he was no longer styled Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: 」Because Zonggan had saved the dynasty, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Liao — but his descendants and daughters were all reduced in rank. Zhen's wife became county mistress of Yongping; Zhen fell from Director with Threefold Parity to Special Grand Master, lost his meng'an, and no longer bore the title of imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 再徙臨潢尹。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to metropolitan guardian of Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again, to guardian of Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 初，與弑熙宗凡九人，海陵以暴虐自斃，秉德、辯、忽土、阿里出虎以疑見殺，言以妻殞，裕、老僧以反誅，至是貞與大興國尚在。

translations.literal: Initially those who joined in assassinating Emperor Xizong numbered nine in all: Hailing perished through his own cruelty and tyranny; Bingde, Bian, Hu Tu, and Aluchuhu were killed on suspicion; Yan died together with his wife; Yu and Laoseng were executed for rebellion — by this time only Zhen and Daxingguo remained.
translations.idiomatic: Of the nine who murdered Emperor Xizong, Hailing had destroyed himself through tyranny; Bingde, Bian, Hu Tu, and Aluchuhu were killed on suspicion; Yan died with his wife; Yu and Laoseng were executed for treason — only Zhen and Daxingguo survived.

sentences.zh: 而興國擯棄不用，獨貞以世姻籍恩寵，雖夫婦降削爵號，而世宗慮久遠，終不以私恩曲庇，久之，詔誅貞及其妻與二子慎思、十六，而宥其諸孫。
