translations.literal: Yet Daxingguo was cast aside and unused; only Zhen, through marriage ties, still enjoyed favor — though husband and wife had been demoted and stripped of titles, Emperor Shizong, considering the long term, would not ultimately shield him out of private affection. After a long while an edict ordered the execution of Zhen, his wife, and two sons Shensi and Shiliu, while pardoning all his grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Daxingguo languished in disgrace; only Zhen, by marriage, still enjoyed favor. Though both spouses had lost their titles, Shizong would not indulge him forever — and after long consideration ordered Zhen, his wife, and sons Shensi and Shiliu executed, sparing the grandsons.

sentences.zh: 俄而，興國亦誅，皇統逆黨盡矣。

translations.literal: Before long Daxingguo was also executed, and the Huangtong coup faction was gone entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Daxingguo was executed too, and the Huangtong conspirators were extinct.

sentences.zh: 李老僧

translations.literal: Li Laoseng
translations.idiomatic: Li Laoseng

sentences.zh: 李老僧，舊為將軍司書吏，與大興國有親，素相厚。

translations.literal: Li Laoseng had formerly been a clerical officer in the Generals' Office; he was related to Daxingguo and they had long been close.
translations.idiomatic: Li Laoseng had been a clerk in the Generals' Office. Related to Daxingguo, the two had long been close.

sentences.zh: 海陵秉政，興國屬諸海陵，海陵以為省令史。

translations.literal: When Hailing took power, Daxingguo was placed under Hailing's authority; Hailing made him a provincial clerical officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing seized power, Daxingguo came under his command and was made a provincial clerk.

sentences.zh: 及將舉事，使老僧結興國，興國終為海陵取符鑰，納海陵宮中成弑逆者，老僧為之也。

translations.literal: When the plot was to be carried out, he had Laoseng win over Daxingguo; in the end Daxingguo took the tallies and keys for Hailing and admitted Hailing into the palace to accomplish the regicide — Laoseng was the one who made this happen.
translations.idiomatic: When the assassination was planned, Hailing had Laoseng win over Daxingguo. Daxingguo finally surrendered the palace keys and admitted Hailing to commit the murder — Laoseng made it happen.

sentences.zh: 海陵既立，以老僧為同知廣甯尹事，賜錢千萬、絹五百匹、馬牛各二百、羊二千。

translations.literal: Once Hailing was enthroned, he made Laoseng associate metropolitan guardian of Guangning, granting ten million cash, five hundred bolts of silk, two hundred horses and two hundred oxen each, and two thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: After his enthronement Hailing made Laoseng associate guardian of Guangning and rewarded him with ten million cash, five hundred bolts of silk, two hundred horses and oxen apiece, and two thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 久之，海陵惡韓王亨，將殺之，求其罪不可得，遂以亨為廣甯尹，再任老僧同知，使伺察亨，構致其罪。

translations.literal: After a long while Hailing came to hate Prince of Han Heng and wished to kill him, but could find no crime; he therefore made Heng metropolitan guardian of Guangning and reappointed Laoseng as associate guardian, charging them to watch Heng and fabricate a charge against him.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing grew to hate Prince of Han Heng and wanted him dead but could find no crime. He made Heng guardian of Guangning and reappointed Laoseng as his deputy, ordering them to watch Heng and fabricate charges.

sentences.zh: 亨喜博，及至廣甯，常與老僧博，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Heng loved gambling; when he reached Guangning he often gambled with Laoseng and treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Heng loved gambling. At Guangning he often played with Laoseng and treated him with great warmth.

sentences.zh: 老僧由是不忍致亨死罪，遲疑者久之。

translations.literal: Laoseng therefore could not bear to bring Heng to the death penalty and hesitated for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Laoseng could not bring himself to destroy Heng and hesitated for a long time.

sentences.zh: 海陵再使小底訛論促老僧，老僧乃與亨家奴六斤謀，殺亨獄中，語在亨傳。

translations.literal: Hailing again sent the petty attendant Elun to urge Laoseng; Laoseng then conspired with Heng's household slave Liujin to kill Heng in prison — the account is in Heng's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing sent the petty attendant Elun to press him again. Laoseng then plotted with Heng's slave Liujin to murder Heng in prison — the full account appears in Heng's biography.

sentences.zh: 及耶律安禮自廣寧還朝，海陵謂之曰：「孛迭三罪，伏其一已見觖望。

translations.literal: When Yelü Anli returned to court from Guangning, Hailing said to him: "Biedie has three crimes; even confessing to one already shows resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Yelü Anli returned from Guangning, Hailing told him: "Biedie has three crimes — confessing to even one shows his resentment.

sentences.zh: 爾乃梁王故吏，若亨伏辜，必罪及親族，故榜殺之。」

translations.literal: You are a former retainer of the Prince of Liang; if Heng were executed according to law, your clansmen would surely be implicated — therefore he was beaten to death."
translations.idiomatic: You were a retainer of Prince of Liang Zongbi. If Heng had been lawfully executed, your kinsmen would have been implicated — so he was beaten to death instead."

sentences.zh: 海陵以老僧于亨有遲回意，遂降老僧為易州刺史。

translations.literal: Because Hailing believed Laoseng had been slow and hesitant regarding Heng, he demoted Laoseng to prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing judged Laoseng had wavered over Heng and demoted him to prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷同知大興尹，賜名惟忠，改延安府同知，大定二年，與兵部尚書可喜謀反，誅。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to associate metropolitan guardian of Daxing, granted the name Weizhong, and changed to associate prefect of Yan'an; in the second year of Dading he joined Minister of War Kexi in plotting rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made associate guardian of Daxing, given the name Weizhong, then associate prefect of Yan'an. In Dading 2 he joined Minister of War Kexi in a rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 論曰：《書》曰：「王左右常伯、常任、准人、綴衣、虎賁。

translations.literal: Commentary: The Book of Documents says: "At the king's left and right are the regular ministers, regular administrators, assessors, robe-bearers, and tiger guards.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Book of Documents says, "At the king's side stand the regular ministers, administrators, assessors, robe-bearers, and tiger guards.

sentences.zh: 周公曰：嗚呼，休茲知恤，鮮哉！」

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou said: Alas — to truly understand this care is rare indeed!"
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou said: Alas, how rare is the man who truly grasps this principle of care!"

sentences.zh: 穆王告伯冏曰：「慎簡乃僚，其無以巧言令色、便辟側媚，其惟起士。」

translations.literal: 」King Mu told Bo Jiong: "Choose your subordinates with care; have none who use clever speech and fair countenance, who are glib and fawning by your side — only men of upright character."
translations.idiomatic: 」King Mu told Bo Jiong: "Choose your officers carefully. Reject men of smooth words and pleasing faces, the glib and the fawning — seek only men of character."

sentences.zh: 金人所謂寢殿小底猶周之綴衣，所謂護衛猶周之虎賁也，則皆群僕侍御之臣矣。

translations.literal: 」What the Jurchen call petty attendants of the sleeping hall corresponds to the Zhou robe-bearers; what they call palace guards corresponds to the Zhou tiger guards — all are throngs of servant-attendants attending upon the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Jin "petty attendants of the sleeping hall" correspond to the Zhou robe-bearers; their "palace guards" to the Zhou tiger guards — all mere servant-attendants of the throne.

sentences.zh: 海陵弑逆，而大興國、忽土、阿里出虎為之扼擘，皆出於小底護衛之中，熙宗固不知恤之也。

translations.literal: Hailing's regicide was executed with Daxingguo, Hu Tu, and Aluchuhu gripping arms to assist — all drawn from among the petty attendants and guards; Emperor Xizong plainly did not understand how to care for such matters.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing's murder was carried out by Daxingguo, Hu Tu, and Aluchuhu — all drawn from the petty attendants and guards. Emperor Xizong clearly failed to govern them with care.

sentences.zh: 一日，熙宗與近侍飲酒，會夜，稽古殿火，上欲往視，都點檢辭不失引帝裾止之，奏曰：「臣在此，陛下何患，願無親往。」

translations.literal: One day Emperor Xizong was drinking with intimate attendants; at nightfall a fire broke out at the Hall of Archaic Study, and the emperor wished to go see for himself. Chief Inspector Cibushi took hold of the emperor's robe to stop him and memorialized: "Your servant is here — what is Your Majesty to fear? I beg you not to go in person."
translations.idiomatic: One night Xizong was drinking with his attendants when the Hall of Archaic Study caught fire. He started to go himself, but chief inspector Cibushi seized his robe and pleaded: "I am here — what danger threatens Your Majesty? Do not go yourself."

sentences.zh: 熙宗謂辭不失被酒，甚怒之，明日，杖而出之，已而思其忠，復見召用。

translations.literal: 」Emperor Xizong thought Cibushi was drunk and was greatly angered; the next day he had him beaten and dismissed. Before long, reflecting on his loyalty, he summoned him back to office.
translations.idiomatic: 」Xizong thought Cibushi drunk and flew into a rage. The next day he had him beaten and expelled — then, remembering his loyalty, recalled him to service.

sentences.zh: 海陵與唐括辯時時屏人私語，護衛特思察其非常，海陵擠而殺之。

translations.literal: Hailing and Tangguo Bian often dismissed others to whisper in private; guard Tesi detected their irregular conduct, and Hailing forced him out and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing and Tangguo Bian constantly dismissed attendants to whisper together. Guard Tesi sensed something wrong — Hailing drove him out and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 皇統末年，群臣解體，無尊君謹上之心，而群奸竊發，僕禦之臣不復有如辭不失、特思者矣。

translations.literal: In the last years of Huangtong the courtiers fell apart, with no heart of reverence for the sovereign or deference to superiors; treacherous men secretly acted, and among servant-attendants there were no longer any like Cibushi and Tesi.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Huangtong the court had lost all reverence for the throne. Conspirators moved in darkness, and no servant-attendant of Cibushi's or Tesi's caliber remained.

sentences.zh: 《綿》之詩曰：「予曰有疏附，予曰有先後，予曰有奔走，予曰有禦侮。」

translations.literal: The Ode "Mian" says: "I said we have distant adherents; I said we have near ones; I said we have runners; I said we have defenders against insult."
translations.idiomatic: The ode "Mian" says: "I spoke of distant supporters, of close allies, of messengers, of defenders against affront."

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，先後禦侮之臣，豈可少哉！

translations.literal: 」Alas — ministers near and far who defend against insult — how can they ever be few!
translations.idiomatic: 」Alas, ministers who stand near the throne and ward off danger — can they ever be too many?

sentences.zh: 完顏元宜

translations.literal: Wanyan Yuanyi
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Yuanyi

sentences.zh: 完顏元宜，本名阿列，一名移特輦，本姓耶律氏。

translations.literal: Wanyan Yuanyi, original name Alie, also called Yitelian, was originally of the Yelü clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Yuanyi, born Alie and also known as Yitelian, was originally of the Yelü clan.

sentences.zh: 父慎思，天輔七年，宗望追遼主至天德，慎思來降，且言夏人以兵迎遼主，將渡河去。

translations.literal: His father Shensi — in the seventh year of Tianfu, when Zongwang pursued the Liao sovereign to Tiande, Shensi came over in surrender and reported that the Western Xia were receiving the Liao sovereign with troops and were about to ferry him across the river to leave.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shensi surrendered when Zongwang pursued the Liao emperor to Tiande in Tianfu 7 (1123), reporting that the Tangut were escorting the Liao emperor across the river to safety.

sentences.zh: 宗望移書夏人諭以禍福，夏人乃止。

translations.literal: Zongwang sent a letter to the Western Xia explaining the gains and losses, and the Western Xia then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang wrote to the Tangut explaining the consequences, and they desisted.

sentences.zh: 賜慎思姓完顏氏，官至儀同三司。

translations.literal: Shensi was granted the surname Wanyan and rose in office to Director with Threefold Parity.
translations.idiomatic: Shensi received the Wanyan surname and rose to Director with Threefold Parity.

sentences.zh: 海陵伐宋，以本官領神武軍都總管，以大名路騎兵萬餘益之。

translations.literal: When Hailing campaigned against Song, with his existing office he took command as chief commander of the Divine Martial Army, augmented by more than ten thousand cavalry of the Daming Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing attacked Song, Yuanyi commanded the Divine Martial Army with more than ten thousand Daming cavalry added to his force.

sentences.zh: 前鋒渡淮，拔昭關，遇宋兵萬餘於柘皋，力戰卻之。

translations.literal: The vanguard crossed the Huai, captured Zhaoguan, and encountered more than ten thousand Song troops at Zhegao; after fierce fighting they drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard crossed the Huai, took Zhaoguan, and at Zhegao routed more than ten thousand Song troops after a hard fight.

sentences.zh: 至和州，宋兵十萬來拒，元宜麾軍力戰，抵暮而罷。

translations.literal: At Hezhou a hundred thousand Song troops came to resist; Yuanyi commanded the army in fierce battle until dusk before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: At Hezhou a hundred thousand Song soldiers barred his path. Yuanyi fought hard until nightfall.

sentences.zh: 宋人乘夜襲營，元宜擊走之，黎明追及宋兵，斬首數萬，以功遷銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The Song attacked the camp by night; Yuanyi struck and drove them off, and at dawn pursued the Song army, beheading tens of thousands; for his merit he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces raided by night; Yuanyi drove them off and at dawn pursued them, taking tens of thousands of heads. He was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 海陵增置浙西道都統制，使元宜領之，督諸軍渡江，佩金牌，賜衣一襲。

translations.literal: Hailing added a chief command of the Zhexi Circuit and had Yuanyi lead it, supervising the armies in crossing the Yangzi; he wore a gold tablet and was granted one suit of clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing created the Zhexi chief command and put Yuanyi in charge of the river crossing, granting him a gold tablet and a suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 十月乙未黎明，元宜、王祥與武勝軍都總管徒單守素、猛安唐括烏野、謀克斡盧保、婁薛、溫都長壽等率眾犯御營。

translations.literal: At dawn on yimwei of the tenth month, Yuanyi, Wang Xiang, chief commander of the Victorious Martial Army Tudan Shousu, meng'an Tangguo Wuye, company captain Walubao, Lou Xue, Wendu Changshou, and others led troops in assault on the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on yimwei of the tenth month, Yuanyi and Wang Xiang joined Tudan Shousu, Tangguo Wuye, Walubao, Lou Xue, Wendu Changshou, and others in attacking the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 海陵聞亂，以為宋兵奄至，攬衣遽起，箭入帳中，取視之，愕然曰：「乃我兵也。」

translations.literal: Hailing heard the disturbance and thought Song troops had suddenly arrived; he grabbed his clothes and sprang up. An arrow entered the tent; he took it and looked, and said in astonishment: "These are my own troops."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the commotion, Hailing thought Song forces had struck. He leaped up — an arrow flew into the tent. He inspected it and exclaimed in shock: "These are my own men."

sentences.zh: 大慶山曰：「事急矣，當出避之。」

translations.literal: 」Da Qing Shan said: "The situation is urgent — you must go out and flee."
translations.idiomatic: 」Da Qing Shan said: "This is desperate — you must flee."

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「走將安往。」

translations.literal: 」Hailing said: "If I flee, where shall I go?"
translations.idiomatic: 」Hailing said: "Flee — to where?"

sentences.zh: 方取弓，已中箭僕地。

translations.literal: 」Just as he was reaching for his bow, he was already struck by an arrow and fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: 」As he reached for his bow, an arrow struck him down.

sentences.zh: 延安少尹納合斡魯補先刃之，手足猶動，遂縊殺之。

translations.literal: Assistant metropolitan guardian of Yan'an Nahe Walubu first cut him with a blade; his hands and feet still moved, and he was then strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yan'an deputy guardian Nahe Walubu struck first with his blade. Hailing's limbs still twitched — they strangled him to finish the job.

sentences.zh: 驍騎指揮使大磐整兵來救，王祥出語之曰：「無及矣。」

translations.literal: The brave-cavalry commander Dapan marshaled troops to rescue him; Wang Xiang went out and told him: "It is too late."
translations.idiomatic: Brave-cavalry commander Dapan rallied troops to rescue him. Wang Xiang came out and said: "Too late."

sentences.zh: 大磐乃止。

translations.literal: 」Dapan then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: 」Dapan halted.

sentences.zh: 軍士攘取行營服用皆盡，乃取大磐衣巾裹海陵屍，焚之。

translations.literal: The soldiers snatched and consumed all the traveling camp's clothing and gear; then they took Dapan's garments and headcloth to wrap Hailing's corpse and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers looted the camp bare. They wrapped Hailing's body in Dapan's clothes and burned it.

sentences.zh: 遂收尚書右丞李通、浙西道副統制郭安國、監軍徒單永年、近侍局使梁珫、副使大慶山，皆殺之。

translations.literal: They then arrested Right Vice Grand Councilor Li Tong, Zhexi deputy chief commander Guo Anguo, army supervisor Tudan Yongnian, director of the Bureau of Intimate Attendance Liang Qiu, and deputy director Da Qing Shan — all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: They seized vice grand councilor Li Tong, Zhexi deputy commander Guo Anguo, army supervisor Tudan Yongnian, intimate attendant director Liang Qiu, and deputy director Da Qing Shan — and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 元宜行左領軍副大都督事，使使者殺皇太子光英于南京。

translations.literal: Yuanyi acted as left army lieutenant vice commander-in-chief and sent envoys to kill Crown Prince Guangying at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi served as acting left army vice commander-in-chief and sent agents to murder Crown Prince Guangying at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 大軍北還。

translations.literal: The great army returned north.
translations.idiomatic: The main army marched north.

sentences.zh: 大定二年春，入見，拜御史大夫，詔曰：「高楨為御史大夫，號為正直，頗涉煩碎，臣下衣冠不正亦被糾舉。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Dading he had audience upon entering court and was appointed Censor-in-Chief; the edict said: "Gao Zhen as Censor-in-Chief was known as upright, yet he was rather finicky — even when subordinates' caps and robes were out of place he would impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Dading 2 he had audience and was made censor-in-chief. The edict read: "Gao Zhen was known for integrity but grew finicky — even crooked caps earned his censure.

sentences.zh: 職事有大於此者，爾宜勉之。」

translations.literal: There are duties greater than this — you should exert yourself in them."
translations.idiomatic: Greater duties await — apply yourself to them."

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜平章政事，封冀國公。

translations.literal: 」Before long he was appointed Grand Councilor of the Peaceful Administration and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: 」Soon he was made grand councilor and enfeoffed Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 賜玉帶、甲第一區，復賜姓完顏氏。

translations.literal: A jade belt and one first-class residence were granted, and he was again given the surname Wanyan.
translations.idiomatic: He received a jade belt, a top-ranked mansion, and the Wanyan surname once more.

sentences.zh: 往泰州路規措討契丹事，元宜使忠勇校尉李榮招窩斡，窩斡殺榮，詔追贈榮進官四階。

translations.literal: Sent to the Taizhou Circuit to plan the campaign against the Khitan, Yuanyi had the loyal-and-brave guard officer Li Rong summon Wohuo; Wohuo killed Rong, and an edict posthumously advanced Rong four ranks in office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi was sent to Taizhou to organize the campaign against the Khitan. He dispatched guard officer Li Rong to summon Wohuo, who killed Rong. Rong was posthumously promoted four ranks.

sentences.zh: 五月，上聞元宜將還，遣使止之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, when the emperor heard Yuanyi was about to return, he sent envoys to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, hearing Yuanyi was heading back, the emperor sent orders to stay him.

sentences.zh: 契丹已平、元宜還朝，奏請益諸群牧鎧甲。

translations.literal: Once the Khitan rebellion was pacified Yuanyi returned to court and memorialized requesting additional armor for all the horse herds.
translations.idiomatic: After the Khitan revolt was crushed Yuanyi returned and asked for more armor for the horse herds.

sentences.zh: 詔從之，每群牧益二十副。

translations.literal: An edict approved this; each horse herd was increased by twenty sets.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed — twenty additional sets per herd.

sentences.zh: 元宜復請益臨潢戍軍士馬，詔給馬六百匹。

translations.literal: Yuanyi again requested additional horses for the garrison troops at Linhuang; an edict granted six hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi also requested more horses for the Linhuang garrison and received six hundred.

sentences.zh: 久之，罷為東京留守。

translations.literal: After a long while he was dismissed and made guardian of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually relieved and made guardian of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 乞還所賜甲第，上從之，賜以襲衣、吐鶻、廄馬、海東青鶻。

translations.literal: He begged to return the granted first-class residence; the emperor consented and granted him ceremonial robes, gyrfalcon ornaments, stable horses, and eastern-sea green gyrfalcons.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the granted mansion; the emperor accepted and gave him court robes, gyrfalcon fittings, stable horses, and eastern-sea falcons.

sentences.zh: 未幾，致仕，薨於家。

translations.literal: Before long he retired from office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He retired soon after and died at home.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，遣使致祭，賻贈甚厚。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he sent envoys to offer sacrifices, with generous funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to mourn him with lavish funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 大定十一年，尚書省奏擬納合斡魯補除授，上曰：「昔廢海陵，此人首入弑之，人臣之罪莫大於是，豈可復加官使？

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dading the Imperial Secretariat memorialized proposing an appointment for Nahe Walubu; the emperor said: "When Hailing was overthrown, this man was the first to enter and assassinate him — no crime of a subject is greater. How can he be further promoted?
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 11 the Imperial Secretariat proposed promoting Nahe Walubu. The emperor said: "When Hailing was overthrown, this man struck first. No subject's crime is greater — how can he be promoted again?

sentences.zh: 其世襲謀克姑聽仍舊。」

translations.literal: His hereditary company captaincy may for the present be left as before."
translations.idiomatic: Let his hereditary company captaincy stand for now."

sentences.zh: 大定十八年，紮里海上言：「凡為人臣能捍災禦侮有功者，宜錄用之。

translations.literal: 」In the eighteenth year of Dading Zhali Hai submitted a memorial: "Any subject who can ward off disaster and repel insult with merit ought to be recorded and employed.
translations.idiomatic: 」In Dading 18 Zhali Hai memorialized: "Subjects who defend the throne against disaster and insult deserve recognition and office.

sentences.zh: 今弑海陵者以為有功，賞以高爵，非所以勸事君也。

translations.literal: Now those who assassinated Hailing are regarded as having merit and rewarded with high ennoblement — this is not how to encourage service to one's lord.
translations.idiomatic: Those who killed Hailing were rewarded with high rank — this does not encourage loyal service.

sentences.zh: 宜削奪，以為人臣之戒。

translations.literal: Their rewards should be revoked, to serve as a warning to subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Strip those rewards away as a warning to all subjects.

sentences.zh: 臣在當時亦與其党，如正名定罪，請自臣始。」

translations.literal: Your servant at the time was also among their faction; if guilt is to be named and fixed, I beg that it begin with me."
translations.idiomatic: I was among them. If accounts must be settled, begin with me."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「紮里海自請其罪以勸事君，此亦人之所難。」

translations.literal: 」The emperor said: "Zhali Hai voluntarily claims his guilt to encourage service to one's lord — this too is what men find difficult."
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor said: "Zhali Hai takes blame upon himself to teach loyalty — that is rare."

sentences.zh: 遂以紮里海充趙王府祗候郎君。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon Zhali Hai was made attendant gentleman of the Zhao Prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: 」Zhali Hai was made attendant in the Zhao Prince's household.

sentences.zh: 元宜子習涅阿補，大定二十五年為符寶祗候，乞依女直人例遷官，上曰：「賜姓一時之權宜。」

translations.literal: Yuanyi's son Xinie Abu — in the twenty-fifth year of Dading, as keeper of the imperial seals and tally attendant, he begged promotion according to the Jurchen precedent; the emperor said: "The granting of the surname was a temporary expedient."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi's son Xinie Abu, a seal keeper in Dading 25, asked for promotion under Jurchen rules. The emperor replied: "The surname was a temporary honor."

sentences.zh: 令習涅阿補還本姓。

translations.literal: 」Xinie Abu was ordered to revert to his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was ordered to resume his original surname.

sentences.zh: 論曰：《春秋》書「齊公子商人弑其君舍」，又曰：「齊人弑其君商人。」

translations.literal: Commentary: The Spring and Autumn Annals records "The son of Duke Shang of Qi, Shangren, murdered his lord She," and again "The men of Qi murdered their lord Shangren."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Spring and Autumn Annals reads, "Qi duke's son Shangren murdered his ruler She," and again, "The men of Qi murdered their ruler Shangren."

sentences.zh: 嗟乎，弑舍者商人也，弑商人者邴埸、閻職也。

translations.literal: 」Alas — the one who murdered She was Shangren, and those who murdered Shangren were Bing Yi and Yan Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: 」Alas — Shangren killed She, and Bing Yi and Yan Zhi killed Shangren.

sentences.zh: 海陵弑熙宗，完顏元宜弑海陵。

translations.literal: Hailing murdered Emperor Xizong; Wanyan Yuanyi murdered Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing murdered Xizong; Wanyan Yuanyi murdered Hailing.

sentences.zh: 商人之弑也，邴埸、閻職去之。

translations.literal: When Shangren was murdered, Bing Yi and Yan Zhi departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shangren fell, Bing Yi and Yan Zhi departed.

sentences.zh: 海陵之弑也，元宜歸於世宗。

translations.literal: When Hailing was murdered, Yuanyi returned to Emperor Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing fell, Yuanyi returned to Shizong.

sentences.zh: 邴、閻賤役，元宜都將也，握君之親兵，窺利以弑之，其罪豈容誅乎，世宗僅能不大用之而已。

translations.literal: Bing and Yan were menial servants; Yuanyi was a commandant of the capital guard who controlled the ruler's personal troops and, seeing an opportunity, murdered him — how could such a crime not be punished by death? Shizong could barely manage no more than refraining from employing him prominently.
translations.idiomatic: Bing and Yan were lowly servants; Yuanyi commanded the capital guard, held the ruler's personal troops, and murdered him when he saw his chance. A crime like that surely deserved death — yet Shizong could do no more than keep him from high office.

sentences.zh: 紮里海猶殺人而自首者也，在律，殺人未聞准首免罪而又予賞者也，況弑逆乎。

translations.literal: Zhali Hai even killed a man and turned himself in; in the law, for homicide one never hears of confession being grounds to waive guilt and moreover grant reward — how much less for regicide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhali Hai killed a man and then surrendered himself. The law never exempts murder on confession, let alone rewards it — and this was regicide.

sentences.zh: 海陵弑五十三年，得有胡沙虎之事。

translations.literal: Fifty-three years after Hailing's murder came the affair of Hu Shahu.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-three years after Hailing's murder came Hu Shahu.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈執中

translations.literal: Geshilie Zhizhong
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie Zhizhong

sentences.zh: 紇石烈執中，本名胡沙虎，阿疏裔孫也。

translations.literal: Geshilie Zhizhong, original name Hu Shahu, was a descendant of Ashu.
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie Zhizhong, born Hu Shahu, was a descendant of Ashu.

sentences.zh: 徙東平路猛安。

translations.literal: He was relocated to a meng'an post in Dongping Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was moved to a meng'an in Dongping Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大定八年，充皇太子護衛，出職太子僕丞，改鷹坊直長，再遷鷹坊使、拱衛直指揮使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dading, he served as a guard of the crown prince, then left that office to become deputy director of the crown prince's stables; he was changed to chief of the hawk-falcon office, and was again promoted to commissioner of the hawk-falcon office and commanding general of the Direct Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 8 he joined the crown prince's guard, then served as deputy director of the crown prince's stables. He became chief of the hawk-falcon office, then commissioner of that office and commanding general of the Direct Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 明昌四年，使過阻居，監酒官移剌保迎謁後時，飲以酒，酒味薄，執中怒，毆傷移剌保，詔的決五十。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Mingchang, on an embassy he passed through Zuju; Yelü Bao, the wine supervisor, was late in coming out to receive him and offered him wine, but the wine was weak. Zhizhong was angered, beat and injured Yelü Bao, and was ordered to receive fifty blows with the rod.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 4, while on embassy duty he passed through Zuju. The wine supervisor Yelü Bao came out late to greet him and served weak wine. Zhizhong flew into a rage, beat Yelü Bao, and was sentenced to fifty strokes of the rod.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷右副點檢，肆傲不奉職，降肇州防禦使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to right vice director of the palace guards; he was arrogantly negligent of his duties and was demoted to defensive commissioner of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made right vice director of the palace guards, but his arrogance and neglect of duty earned him demotion to defensive commissioner of Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 逾年，遷興平軍節度使。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to military governor of Xingping Army.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed military governor of Xingping Army.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起復歸德軍節度使，改開遠軍兼西南路招討副使。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he entered mourning, but was recalled from mourning to serve as military governor of Guide Army; he was changed to Kaiyuan Army and concurrently vice pacification commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he entered mourning, but was recalled to serve as military governor of Guide Army, then transferred to Kaiyuan Army as vice pacification commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.

sentences.zh: 俄知大名府事。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed prefect of Daming.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，召為簽樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Cheng'an, he was summoned to serve as signing member of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 2 he was summoned to the Bureau of Military Affairs as a signing member.

sentences.zh: 詔佐丞相襄征伐，執中不欲行，奏曰：「臣與襄有隙，且殺臣矣。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to assist the chief councilor Xiang on campaign; Zhizhong did not wish to go and memorialized: "Your servant has a grudge against Xiang, and he will kill me."
translations.idiomatic: When ordered to assist Chief Councilor Xiang on campaign, Zhizhong refused and memorialized: "I bear a grudge against Xiang — he will kill me."

sentences.zh: 上怒其言不遜，事下有司，既而赦之，出為永定軍節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered by his disrespectful words; the matter was referred to the appropriate offices, but he was soon pardoned and sent out as military governor of Yongding Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, angered by his insolence, referred the matter to the courts, then pardoned him and sent him out as military governor of Yongding Army.

sentences.zh: 改西北路招討使，復為永定軍，坐奪部軍馬解職。

translations.literal: He was changed to pacification commissioner of the Northwest Circuit, then again to Yongding Army; he was dismissed from office for seizing his subordinates' horses and mounts.
translations.idiomatic: He was made pacification commissioner of the Northwest Circuit, then returned to Yongding Army, but was dismissed for seizing his subordinates' horses.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，起知大興府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe, he was reappointed and made prefect of Daxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 1 he was reinstated as prefect of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 詔契丹人立功官賞恩同女直人，許存養馬匹，得充司吏譯人，著為令。

translations.literal: An edict declared that Khitans who achieved merit would receive official rewards and favors equal to Jurchens, would be permitted to keep and raise horses, and could serve as clerks and interpreters — and this was established as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Khitans who earned merit the same rewards as Jurchens, allowed them to keep horses, and permitted them to serve as clerks and interpreters — and made this law.

sentences.zh: 執中格詔不下，上責之曰；

translations.literal: Zhizhong blocked the edict and did not issue it; the emperor reproached him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong withheld the edict. The emperor rebuked him:

sentences.zh: 「汝雖意在防閑，而不知朝廷自有定格，自今勿復如此煩碎生事也。」

translations.literal: "Though your intent was to guard against impropriety, you did not know that the court has its own fixed regulations; from now on do not again be so fussy and stir up trouble in this way."
translations.idiomatic: "You meant to guard against abuse, but the court already has fixed rules. Do not stir up such petty trouble again."

sentences.zh: 乃下詔行之。

translations.literal: The edict was then issued and put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was then promulgated.

sentences.zh: 淶水人魏廷實祖任兒，舊為靳文昭家放良，天德三年，編籍正戶，已三世矣。

translations.literal: Wei Tingshi of Lishui, originally named Ren'er, had formerly been manumitted from the household of Jin Wenzhao; in the third year of Tiande he was registered as a principal household, and this had already passed through three generations.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tingshi of Lishui, born Ren'er, had been freed from bondage in Jin Wenzhao's household. Registered as a principal household in Tiande 3, his family had been free for three generations.

sentences.zh: 文昭孫勍詆廷實為奴，及妄訴毆詈，警巡院鞫對無狀，法當訴本貫。

translations.literal: Wenzhao's grandson Qing slandered Tingshi as a slave and brought a false charge of assault and abuse; the patrol and inspection office examined the case and found no basis — by law the suit should be brought in the home district.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao's grandson Qing called Tingshi a slave and falsely accused him of assault. The patrol office found no case; by law the suit belonged in Tingshi's home district.

sentences.zh: 勍訴於府，執中使廷實納錢五百貫與勍。

translations.literal: Qing sued at the prefectural office; Zhizhong had Tingshi pay five hundred strings of cash to Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Qing brought the suit to the prefecture, and Zhizhong ordered Tingshi to pay Qing five hundred strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 廷實不從，還淶水，執中徑遣鎖致廷實。

translations.literal: Tingshi refused, returned to Lishui, and Zhizhong directly sent men to fetch him in chains.
translations.idiomatic: Tingshi refused, went home to Lishui, and Zhizhong sent men to drag him back in chains.

sentences.zh: 御史臺請移問，執中轉奏御史臺不依制，府未結斷，令移推。

translations.literal: The Censorate requested that the case be transferred for investigation; Zhizhong memorialized in turn that the Censorate was not following regulations — the prefectural office had not yet concluded the case, yet ordered it transferred for reinvestigation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Censorate asked to take the case, Zhizhong countered that it was breaking procedure by demanding a transfer before the prefecture had finished.

sentences.zh: 詔吏部侍郎李柄、戶部侍郎粘割合答推問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Vice Minister of the Civil Service Li Bing and Vice Minister of Revenue Niancan Hedda to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Vice Ministers Li Bing and Niancan Hedda to investigate.

sentences.zh: 炳、合答奏御史臺理直，詔乃切責執中。

translations.literal: Bing and Hedda reported that the Censorate was in the right, and an edict sternly reproached Zhizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Bing and Hedda found for the Censorate, and an edict sharply rebuked Zhizhong.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞孟鑄奏彈執中「貪殘專恣，不奉法令。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Meng Zhu memorialized impeaching Zhizhong: "Greedy and cruel, arbitrary and willful, he does not obey laws and edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Meng Zhu impeached Zhizhong: "He is greedy, cruel, and lawless — he defies every statute.

sentences.zh: 釋罪之後，累過不悛。

translations.literal: After being released from punishment, he repeatedly offended without reform.
translations.idiomatic: After each pardon he offended again without repentance.

sentences.zh: 既蒙恩貸，轉生跋扈。

translations.literal: Having received imperial grace and pardon, he grew all the more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Spared by imperial grace, he grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 如雄州詐認馬，平州冒支俸，破魏廷實家。

translations.literal: Such as falsely claiming horses at Xiong Prefecture, drawing salaries fraudulently at Ping Prefecture, and ruining Wei Tingshi's household.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely claimed horses at Xiong Prefecture, drew pay he was not owed at Ping Prefecture, and ruined Wei Tingshi's household.

sentences.zh: 發其塚墓，拜表不赴，祈雨聚妓，毆詈同僚擅令停職，失師帥之體，不稱京尹之任」。

translations.literal: Disturbing ancestral tombs, failing to attend when summoned by memorial, gathering courtesans while praying for rain, beating and reviling colleagues and arbitrarily ordering their suspension from office — losing the bearing befitting a military commander, unworthy of the post of capital prefect."
translations.idiomatic: He opened graves, ignored summonses, gathered courtesans while praying for rain, beat and reviled colleagues and suspended them at will — conduct unworthy of a commander or a capital prefect."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「執中粗人，似有跋扈爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zhizhong is a coarse man — he merely seems overbearing, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Zhizhong is a rough man — a little overbearing, nothing more."

sentences.zh: 鑄對曰：「明天子在上，豈容有跋扈之臣。」

translations.literal: Zhu replied: "With an enlightened Son of Heaven above, how could an overbearing minister be tolerated?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu answered: "With an enlightened ruler on the throne, how can an overbearing minister be tolerated?"

sentences.zh: 上意寤，取閱奏章，詔尚書省問之。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was awakened; he took up and read the memorial, and ordered the Department of State Affairs to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the point, read the memorial himself, and ordered the Department of State Affairs to investigate.

sentences.zh: 由是改武衛軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was changed to commanding general of the Martial Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to commanding general of the Martial Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 平章政事僕散揆宣撫河南，執中除山東東西路統軍使。

translations.literal: Chief councilor of the fourth rank Pusan Kai was appointed to pacify Henan; Zhizhong was appointed overall military commander of the East and West Shandong Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Councilor Pusan Kai was sent to pacify Henan, Zhizhong was made overall military commander of eastern and western Shandong.

sentences.zh: 揆行省汴京伐宋，升諸道統軍司為兵馬都統府，執中為山東兩路兵馬都統，定海軍節度使完顏撒剌副之。

translations.literal: Kai established a branch secretariat at Bianjing to campaign against Song; the various circuit overall military command offices were elevated to armies-and-horses supreme command prefectures; Zhizhong became supreme commander of the two Shandong circuits, with Wanyan Sala, military governor of Dinghai Army, as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Kai set up a branch secretariat at Bianjing to attack Song, elevated circuit commands to supreme army headquarters, and made Zhizhong supreme commander of the two Shandong routes, with Wanyan Sala of Dinghai Army as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 執中分兵駐金城、朐山，請益發東平路兵屯密、沂、寧海、登、萊以遏兵沖，詔從之，時泰和六年四月也。

translations.literal: Zhizhong divided his forces and garrisoned Jincheng and Qushan; he requested additional troops from Dongping Circuit to be stationed at Mi, Yi, Ninghai, Deng, and Lai to block the enemy's thrust — the edict approved this; it was the fourth month of the sixth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong split his forces between Jincheng and Qushan and asked for more Dongping troops at Mi, Yi, Ninghai, Deng, and Lai to block the enemy advance. The request was granted — it was the fourth month of Taihe 6.

sentences.zh: 五月，宋兵犯金城，執中遣巡檢使周奴以騎兵三百禦之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Song troops attacked Jincheng; Zhizhong sent the patrol commissioner Zhounu with three hundred cavalry to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Song forces struck Jincheng. Zhizhong sent Patrol Commissioner Zhounu with three hundred horsemen to meet them.

sentences.zh: 會宋益兵轉趨沭陽，謀克三合伏卒五十人篁竹中，伺宋兵過突出擊之，殺十數人，追至縣城，宋兵不敢出。

translations.literal: When Song reinforced and turned toward Shuyang, the commander Sanhe ambushed fifty soldiers in bamboo groves; as the Song troops passed he burst out and struck them, killing more than ten, pursued them to the county seat, and the Song troops did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: When Song reinforcements swung toward Shuyang, Commander Sanhe hid fifty men in bamboo thickets, sprang out as they passed, killed more than ten, and chased them to the county seat until they dared not emerge.

sentences.zh: 會周奴以兵入城，宋兵逾城走，三合已焚其舟，合擊大破之，斬首五百餘級，殺宋統領李藻，擒忠義軍將呂璋。

translations.literal: When Zhounu entered the city with troops, the Song troops fled over the walls; Sanhe had already burned their boats, and in combined attack they thoroughly defeated them, beheading more than five hundred, killing the Song commander Li Zao, and capturing the Loyal and Righteous Army general Lü Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhounu entered the city; the Song troops fled over the walls. Sanhe had already burned their boats, and together they routed the enemy — more than five hundred heads, Song commander Li Zao killed, and Loyal and Righteous Army general Lü Zhang captured.

sentences.zh: 十月，執中率兵二萬出清口，宋以步騎萬餘列南岸，戰艦百艘拒上流，相持累日。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Zhizhong led twenty thousand troops out from Qingkou; Song deployed more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry on the south bank, with a hundred warships blocking the upper stream — they faced off for many days.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhizhong led twenty thousand men from Qingkou. Song lined more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry on the south bank and blocked the upper stream with a hundred warships. The two sides faced each other for days.

sentences.zh: 執中以舟兵二千搏戰，遏宋舟兵，遣副統移剌古與涅率精騎四千自下流徑渡。

translations.literal: Zhizhong used two thousand naval troops to grapple in battle and hold back the Song fleet, while dispatching vice commander Yelü Guyuni with four thousand elite cavalry to cross directly from the lower stream.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong pinned the Song fleet with two thousand boatmen while Vice Commander Yelü Guyuni led four thousand elite cavalry across downstream.

sentences.zh: 宋兵望騎兵登南岸，水陸俱潰。

translations.literal: The Song troops saw the cavalry ascend the south bank, and both land and water forces collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song saw cavalry reach the south bank, their land and river forces collapsed together.

sentences.zh: 追斬及溺死者甚眾，盡獲其戰艦及戰馬三百，遂克淮陰，進兵圍楚州。

translations.literal: Those pursued and killed or drowned were extremely numerous; they captured all the warships and three hundred war horses, then took Huaiyin and advanced to besiege Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The slaughter by blade and drowning was immense. They seized every warship and three hundred horses, took Huaiyin, and marched to besiege Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷元帥左監軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left supervising general of the marshals.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left supervising general of the marshals.

sentences.zh: 執中縱兵虜掠，上聞之，杖其經歷官阿里不孫，放還所掠。

translations.literal: Zhizhong let his troops plunder; when the emperor heard of it, he had his staff officer Alibusun beaten and ordered the plunder returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong let his men loot freely. When the emperor learned of it, he had Zhizhong's staff officer Alibusun beaten and the loot restored.

sentences.zh: 未幾，宋人請和，詔罷兵。

translations.literal: Before long the Song sought peace, and an edict halted the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Song sued for peace, and the throne ordered the armies withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 除西南路招討使，改西京留守。

translations.literal: He was appointed pacification commissioner of the Southwest Circuit and then changed to defender of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was made pacification commissioner of the Southwest Circuit, then defender of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 大安元年，授世襲謀克，復知大興府事，出知太原府，復為西京留守，行樞密院，兼安撫使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Da'an, he was granted hereditary commander status, again made prefect of Daxing, then sent out as prefect of Taiyuan, again defender of the Western Capital, acting Bureau of Military Affairs, and concurrently pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Da'an 1 he received hereditary commander status, served again as prefect of Daxing, then Taiyuan, then Western Capital defender, acting head of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以勁兵七千遇大兵，戰于定安之北，薄暮，先以麾下遁去。

translations.literal: With seven thousand crack troops he encountered the great army and fought north of Ding'an; at dusk he fled first with his personal followers.
translations.idiomatic: With seven thousand picked troops he met the Mongols north of Ding'an. At dusk he fled first with his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 眾遂潰。

translations.literal: The army then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The army then broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 行次蔚州，擅取官庫銀五千兩及衣幣諸物，奪官民馬，與從行私人入紫荊關，杖殺淶水令。

translations.literal: En route at Yu Prefecture, he on his own authority took five thousand taels of silver from the government treasury and various cloth and goods, seized government and civilian horses, entered Zijing Pass with private followers in his retinue, and beat to death the magistrate of Lishui.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Yu Prefecture he seized five thousand taels of silver from the treasury, cloth and goods, government and civilian horses, entered Zijing Pass with private followers, and beat the magistrate of Lishui to death.

sentences.zh: 至中都，朝廷皆不問。

translations.literal: When he reached the Central Capital, the court asked nothing about any of it.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the Central Capital, the court asked no questions.

sentences.zh: 乃遷右副元帥，權尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was then promoted to right vice marshal and acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made right vice marshal and acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 執中益無所忌憚，自請步騎二萬屯宣德州，與之三千，令駐媯川。

translations.literal: Zhizhong grew all the more without fear or restraint; he requested twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Xuande Prefecture — he was given three thousand and ordered to encamp at Guichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong grew bolder still. He asked for twenty thousand infantry and cavalry at Xuande Prefecture; he was given three thousand and told to camp at Guichuan.

sentences.zh: 崇慶元年正月，執中乞移屯南口或屯新莊，移文尚書省曰：「大兵來必不能支，一身不足惜，三千兵為可憂，十二關、建春、萬甯宮且不保。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Chongqing, Zhizhong begged to move his encampment to Nankou or Xinnzhuang; he sent a dispatch to the Department of State Affairs saying: "When the great army comes we surely cannot hold — one man's body is not worth sparing, but the three thousand troops are worrisome; the Twelve Passes, Jianchun, and Wanníng Palace will not even be safe."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chongqing 1, Zhizhong asked to move to Nankou or Xinnzhuang and wrote the Department of State Affairs: "When the Mongols come we cannot hold. One man's life is nothing — but three thousand troops matter. The Twelve Passes, Jianchun, and Wanníng Palace will not survive."

sentences.zh: 朝廷惡其言，下有司按問，詔數其十五罪，罷歸田里。

translations.literal: The court hated his words; the matter was referred to the appropriate offices for investigation; an edict enumerated fifteen crimes and dismissed him to return to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: The court was outraged. Officials investigated, an edict listed fifteen crimes, and he was dismissed to his home.

sentences.zh: 明年，復召至中都，預議軍事。

translations.literal: The next year he was again summoned to the Central Capital to participate in deliberations on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recalled to the Central Capital to join military deliberations.

sentences.zh: 左諫議大夫張行信上書曰：「胡沙虎專逞私意，不循公道，蔑省部以示強梁，媚近臣以求稱譽，骫法行事，枉害平民。

translations.literal: Left remonstrance grandee Zhang Xingxin submitted a memorial saying: "Hu Shahu indulges his private will alone, does not follow the public way, despises the provincial and ministerial offices to show his high-handedness, flatters favorites to seek praise, bends the law in his actions, and wrongly harms common people.
translations.idiomatic: Left Remonstrance Grandee Zhang Xingxin wrote: "Hu Shahu follows only his own will, scorns the ministries to show his power, flatters favorites for praise, bends the law, and wrongs common people.

sentences.zh: 行院山西，出師無律，不戰先退，擅取官物，杖殺縣令。

translations.literal: On the branch secretariat in Shanxi, he took the field without discipline, retreated before fighting, seized government goods on his own authority, and beat a county magistrate to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the Shanxi branch secretariat he marched without discipline, fled before fighting, seized government goods, and beat a county magistrate to death.

sentences.zh: 屯駐媯川，乞移內地，其謀略概可見矣。

translations.literal: Encamped at Guichuan, he begged to move to the interior — his whole strategy is roughly visible.
translations.idiomatic: Camped at Guichuan, he begged to move inland — his intentions are plain enough.

sentences.zh: 欲使改易前非。

translations.literal: To wish him to change his former wrongs—
translations.idiomatic: To expect him to mend his ways—

sentences.zh: 以收後效，不亦難乎。

translations.literal: and reap later merit — would that not be difficult?
translations.idiomatic: and earn future merit — is that not a vain hope?

sentences.zh: 才誠可取，雖在微賤皆當擢用，何必老舊始能立功。

translations.literal: If talent is truly worth taking, even those of humble station should be promoted and employed — why must one be old and long-serving before one can achieve merit?
translations.idiomatic: Worthy talent should be promoted from any rank. Merit does not require age and long service.

sentences.zh: 一將之用，安危所系，惟朝廷加察，天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: The employment of a single general is bound up with safety and peril; may the court examine closely — the realm would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: A general's appointment binds the fate of the realm. I beg the court to look closely — the empire would be the better for it."

sentences.zh: 丞相徒單鎰以為不可用，參知政事絪跪奏其奸惡，乃止。

translations.literal: Chief councilor Tudan Yi deemed him unusable; participation councilor Yin knelt and memorialized his wickedness, and the matter was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Tudan Yi said he was unfit; Participation Councilor Yin knelt and exposed his crimes, and the appointment was stopped.

sentences.zh: 執中善結近幸，交口稱譽。

translations.literal: Zhizhong was good at cultivating favorites; they all praised him in one voice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong cultivated the emperor's favorites, and they praised him in chorus.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔給留守半俸，預議軍事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, an edict granted him half the salary of a defender and participation in military deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month an edict granted him half a defender's salary and a seat in military councils.

sentences.zh: 張行信復諫曰：「伏聞以胡沙虎老臣，欲起而用。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingxin remonstrated again: "I have heard that because Hu Shahu is an old minister, you wish to recall and employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingxin remonstrated again: "I hear that because Hu Shahu is an old minister, you mean to recall him.

sentences.zh: 人之能否，不在新舊。

translations.literal: A man's competence or incompetence does not lie in whether he is new or old.
translations.idiomatic: Ability has nothing to do with seniority.

sentences.zh: 彼向之敗，朝廷既知之矣。

translations.literal: His previous defeat — the court already knows of it.
translations.idiomatic: The court already knows how he failed before.

sentences.zh: 乃復用之，無乃不可乎。」

translations.literal: Yet to employ him again — would that not be inadmissible?"
translations.idiomatic: To employ him again — surely that cannot be right?"

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: And so it was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was halted.

sentences.zh: 上終以執中為可用，賜金牌，權右副元帥，將武衛軍五千人屯中都城北。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately deemed Zhizhong usable; he was granted a gold tablet, made acting right vice marshal, and led five thousand Martial Guard troops to encamp north of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still found Zhizhong usable, granted him a gold tablet, made him acting right vice marshal, and gave him five thousand Martial Guard troops north of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 執中乃與其党經歷官文繡局直長完顏醜奴、提控宿直將軍蒲察六斤、武衛軍鈐轄烏古論奪剌謀作亂。

translations.literal: Zhizhong then joined with his faction — staff officer and direct chief of the Embroidery Bureau Wanyan Chounu, garrison commander and palace guard general Pucha Liujin, and Martial Guard controller Ugulian Duola — to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong then plotted rebellion with his faction: staff officer Wanyan Chounu of the Embroidery Bureau, Garrison Commander and Palace Guard General Pucha Liujin, and Martial Guard Controller Ugulian Duola.

sentences.zh: 是時，大元大兵在近，上使奉職即軍中責執中止務馳獵。

translations.literal: At this time the great army of the Great Yuan was near; the emperor sent a court attendant to the camp to reproach Zhizhong for stopping at nothing but hunting.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongols were near. The emperor sent an attendant to the camp to rebuke Zhizhong for doing nothing but hunt.

sentences.zh: 不恤軍事。

translations.literal: He did not care for military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He neglected military affairs entirely.

sentences.zh: 執中方飼鷂，怒擲殺之，遂妄稱知大興府徒單南平及其子刑部侍郎駙馬都尉沒烈謀反，奉詔討之。

translations.literal: Zhizhong was just feeding a hawk when, in anger, he threw it down and killed it; he then falsely claimed that Daxing Prefect Tudan Nanping and his son, Vice Minister of Justice and imperial son-in-law Moilie, were plotting rebellion, and under pretense of an edict went to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: While feeding a hawk, Zhizhong angrily dashed it to the ground and killed it. He then falsely claimed that Daxing Prefect Tudan Nanping and his son Moilie, vice minister of justice and imperial son-in-law, were plotting rebellion, and marched under pretense of an imperial order to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 南平姻家福海，別將兵屯於城北，遣人以好語招之，福海不知，既至乃執之。

translations.literal: Nanping's in-law Fuhai was separately commanding troops encamped north of the city; Zhizhong sent someone with friendly words to summon him — Fuhai did not know, and once he arrived was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Nanping's in-law Fuhai commanded separate troops north of the city. Zhizhong sent friendly words to summon him; Fuhai came unsuspecting and was seized.

sentences.zh: 八月二十五日未五更，分其軍為三軍，由章義門入，自將一軍由通玄門入。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month, before the fifth watch, he divided his army into three forces entering through Zhangyi Gate; he personally led one force entering through Tongxuan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth of the eighth month, before the fifth watch, he split his army into three columns — two through Zhangyi Gate and one he led through Tongxuan Gate.

sentences.zh: 執中恐城中出兵來拒，乃遣一騎先馳抵東華門大呼曰：「大軍至北關，已接戰矣。」

translations.literal: Zhizhong feared troops would be sent out from the city to resist; he dispatched a rider who galloped first to the Donghua Gate and shouted: "The great army has reached North Gate and battle is already joined!"
translations.idiomatic: Fearing troops would sally from the city, Zhizhong sent a rider galloping to the Donghua Gate to shout: "The enemy has reached North Gate — battle is joined!"

sentences.zh: 既而再遣一騎亦如之。

translations.literal: Then he sent another rider who did the same.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a second rider to repeat the same cry.

sentences.zh: 使徒單金壽召知大興府徒單南平，南平不知，行至廣陽門西富義坊，馬上與執中相見，執中手槍刺之墮馬下，金壽斫殺之。

translations.literal: He had Tudan Jinshou summon Daxing Prefect Tudan Nanping; Nanping did not know, and when he reached Fuyi Ward west of Guangyang Gate and met Zhizhong on horseback, Zhizhong stabbed him with a spear and he fell from his horse; Jinshou hacked him to death.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Tudan Jinshou to summon Daxing Prefect Tudan Nanping. Nanping came unsuspecting to Fuyi Ward west of Guangyang Gate, met Zhizhong on horseback, was speared and thrown from his horse, and Jinshou finished him with a blade.

sentences.zh: 使烏古論奪剌召沒烈，殺之。

translations.literal: He had Ugulian Duola summon Moilie and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ugulian Duola to summon Moilie and killed him.

sentences.zh: 符寶祗候鄯陽、護衛十人長完顏石古乃聞亂，遽召大漢軍五百人赴難，與執中戰不勝，皆死之。

translations.literal: Seal and tally attendant Zhenyang and the ten-man chief of the palace guard Wanyan Shigunai heard of the turmoil and hastily summoned five hundred Great Han Army troops to the rescue; they fought Zhizhong but could not prevail, and all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Seal attendant Zhenyang and Palace Guard decurion Wanyan Shigunai heard of the revolt, mustered five hundred Great Han Army troops, fought Zhizhong, and were all killed.

sentences.zh: 執中至東華門，使呼門者親軍百戶冬兒、五十戶蒲察六斤，皆不應，許以世襲猛安、三品職事官，亦不應。

translations.literal: Zhizhong reached the Donghua Gate and had the gatekeepers called — personal guard centurion Dong'er and fifty-man commander Pucha Liujin — but neither responded; even when promised hereditary meng'an status and third-rank official posts, they still did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: At the Donghua Gate Zhizhong called the gatekeepers — centurion Dong'er and fifty-man commander Pucha Liujin. They would not answer, even when he promised hereditary meng'an rank and third-grade office.

sentences.zh: 呼都點檢徒單渭河，謂河即徒單鎬也。

translations.literal: He called the capital guard director Tudan Weihe — Weihe being Tudan Hao.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Capital Guard Director Tudan Weihe — Weihe was Tudan Hao.

sentences.zh: 渭河縋城出見執中，執中命聚薪焚東華門，立梯登城。

translations.literal: Weihe was lowered by rope from the wall to see Zhizhong; Zhizhong ordered firewood piled to burn the Donghua Gate and ladders set up to ascend the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Weihe was lowered from the wall to meet Zhizhong, who ordered firewood piled to burn the Donghua Gate and ladders raised to scale it.

sentences.zh: 護衛斜烈、乞兒、親軍春山共掊鎖開門納執中。

translations.literal: Palace guards Xielie and Qi'er and personal guard Chunshan together broke the lock and opened the gate to admit Zhizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards Xielie and Qi'er and personal guard Chunshan broke the lock together and opened the gate to Zhizhong.

sentences.zh: 執中入宮，盡以其党易宿衛。

translations.literal: Zhizhong entered the palace and replaced all the palace guards with his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong entered the palace and replaced every palace guard with his own men.

sentences.zh: 自稱監國都元帥，居大興府，陳兵自衛。

translations.literal: He styled himself regent supreme marshal, took up residence at Daxing Prefecture, and deployed troops for his own protection.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself regent supreme marshal, took up residence at Daxing Prefecture, and surrounded himself with troops.

sentences.zh: 急召都轉運使孫椿年取銀幣賞金壽、奪剌及軍官軍士、大興府輿隸。

translations.literal: He urgently summoned Director of Transport Sun Chunnian to fetch silver and goods to reward Jinshou, Duola, and the officers, soldiers, and sedan-chair bearers of Daxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently summoned Transport Director Sun Chunnian to bring silver and goods to reward Jinshou, Duola, the officers and soldiers, and Daxing Prefecture's sedan bearers.

sentences.zh: 是夜，召聲妓與親黨會飲。

translations.literal: That night he summoned singing girls and feasted with his intimate faction.
translations.idiomatic: That night he summoned singing girls and feasted with his confederates.

sentences.zh: 明日，以兵逼上出居衛邸，誘左丞完顏綱至軍中，即殺之。

translations.literal: The next day he used troops to compel the emperor to move out and dwell at the guard residence; he lured Left Vice Director Wanyan Gang to the camp and immediately killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he forced the emperor from the palace to the guard residence, lured Left Vice Director Wanyan Gang to camp, and killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 執中意不可測，丞相徒單鎰勸執中立宣宗，執中然之。

translations.literal: Zhizhong's intentions were unpredictable; Chief Councilor Tudan Yi persuaded Zhizhong to enthroned Emperor Xuanzong, and Zhizhong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong's intentions were unclear. Chief Councilor Tudan Yi persuaded him to enthrone Emperor Xuanzong, and Zhizhong agreed.

sentences.zh: 是時，莊獻太子在中都，執中以皇太子儀仗迎莊獻入居東宮。

translations.literal: At this time Crown Prince Zhuangxian was at the Central Capital; Zhizhong welcomed Zhuangxian with crown prince ceremonial and had him take up residence in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhuangxian was then at the Central Capital. Zhizhong received him with full crown prince ceremony and installed him in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 召符寶郎徒單福壽取符寶，陳於大興府露階上。

translations.literal: He summoned seal attendant Tudan Fushou to fetch the imperial seals and tally, and displayed them on the open steps of Daxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Seal Attendant Tudan Fushou to bring the imperial seals and tallies and displayed them on the open steps of Daxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 盜用御寶出制，除完顏醜奴德州防禦使，烏古論奪剌順天軍節度使，蒲察六斤橫海軍節度使，徒單金壽永定軍節度使，雖除外官，皆留之左右。

translations.literal: He usurped the imperial seals to issue edicts, appointing Wanyan Chounu Defense Commissioner of Dezhou, Ugulian Duola Military Commissioner of the Shuntian Army, Pucha Liujin Military Commissioner of the Henghai Army, and Tudan Jinshou Military Commissioner of the Yongding Army; though he granted them outer posts, he kept them all at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong forged edicts with the imperial seals, appointing Wanyan Chounu defense commissioner of Dezhou, Ugulian Duola military commissioner of the Shuntian Army, Pucha Liujin military commissioner of the Henghai Army, and Tudan Jinshou military commissioner of the Yongding Army — outer offices in name, but all kept at his side.

sentences.zh: 其餘除拜猶數十人。

translations.literal: The rest of the appointments and investitures numbered still several tens of persons.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens more received appointments besides.

sentences.zh: 同時有兩蒲察六斤，其一守東華門不肯從亂者。

translations.literal: At the same time there were two Pucha Liujin; one of them guarded the Donghua Gate and refused to join the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: There were two men named Pucha Liujin at the time; one guarded the Donghua Gate and refused to join the revolt.

sentences.zh: 召禮部令史張好禮欲鑄監國元帥印，好禮曰：「自古無異姓監國者。」

translations.literal: He summoned Ministry of Rites clerk Zhang Haoli, wishing to cast a seal for regent marshal; Haoli said: "From antiquity there has never been a regent of a different surname."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Ministry of Rites clerk Zhang Haoli to cast a regent-marshal seal. Haoli replied: "There has never been a regent who was not of the imperial surname."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: 」And he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: With that he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 遣奉御完顏忽失來等三人，護衛蒲鮮班底、完顏醜奴等十人，迎宣宗於彰德。

translations.literal: He dispatched three palace attendants including Wanyan Huslai, with guards Puxian Bandi, Wanyan Chounu, and ten others, to welcome Emperor Xuanzong at Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: He sent three palace attendants led by Wanyan Huslai, with ten guards including Puxian Bandi and Wanyan Chounu, to welcome Emperor Xuanzong at Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 使宦者李思忠弑上于衛邸。

translations.literal: He had eunuch Li Sizhong assassinate the emperor at the guard residence.
translations.idiomatic: He had the eunuch Li Sizhong murder the emperor at the guard residence.

sentences.zh: 盡撤沿邊諸軍赴中都平州、騎兵屯薊州以自重，邊戍皆不守矣。

translations.literal: He fully withdrew all border armies to the Central Capital and Pingzhou; cavalry encamped at Jizhou to increase his own strength, and frontier garrisons were all abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled every border army back to the Central Capital and Pingzhou, massed cavalry at Jizhou to strengthen his hand, and left the frontier undefended.

sentences.zh: 戊申，執中侍朝，宣宗賜之坐，執中就坐不辭。

translations.literal: On wushen, Zhizhong attended court; Emperor Xuanzong granted him a seat, and Zhizhong took his seat without declining.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Zhizhong attended court. Emperor Xuanzong offered him a seat, and Zhizhong accepted without demur.

sentences.zh: 無何，執中奏請降衛紹王為庶人，奏再上，詔百官議於朝堂。

translations.literal: Before long, Zhizhong memorialized requesting that Prince Shao of Wei be reduced to commoner status; when the memorial was submitted again, an edict ordered the hundred officials to deliberate in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhizhong memorialized to demote Prince Shao of Wei to commoner rank. When he submitted it again, the emperor ordered the court to debate the matter in the hall.

sentences.zh: 太子少傅奧屯忠孝、侍讀學士蒲察思忠附執中議，眾相視莫敢言，獨文學田廷芳奮然曰：「先朝素無失德，尊號在禮不當削。」

translations.literal: Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Aotun Zhongxiao and Reader-in-Waiting Pucha Sizhong sided with Zhizhong's proposal; the crowd looked at one another and none dared speak — only literary officer Tian Tingfang said impassionedly: "The former reign had no moral failings; by ritual his honored title ought not be stripped."
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor Aotun Zhongxiao and Reader-in-Waiting Pucha Sizhong backed Zhizhong. The officials looked at one another in silence until Literary Officer Tian Tingfang spoke up: "The previous emperor was without fault; by ritual his title must not be removed."

sentences.zh: 於是從之者禮部張敬甫、諫議張信甫、戶部武文伯、龐才卿、石抹晉卿等二十四人。

translations.literal: 」Those who then followed numbered twenty-four, including Ministry of Rites Zhang Jingfu, Remonstrance Officer Zhang Xinfu, Ministry of Revenue Wu Wenbo, Pang Caiqing, and Shimojin Jinqi.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four officials sided with him, among them Zhang Jingfu of the Ministry of Rites, Remonstrance Officer Zhang Xinfu, Wu Wenbo of the Ministry of Revenue, Pang Caiqing, and Shimojin Jinqi.

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「辟諸問途，百人曰東行是，十人曰西行是，行道之人果適東乎、適西乎。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said: "If you ask the people of Bi about the road — a hundred say east is right, ten say west is right — does the traveler in fact go east or west?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong said: "As when one asks passersby for directions — a hundred say go east, ten say go west — does the traveler in fact go east or west?

sentences.zh: 豈以百人、十人為是非哉？」

translations.literal: How could one take a hundred or ten people as right or wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: Can right and wrong be settled by counting heads?"

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「朕徐思之。」

translations.literal: 」Then he said: "I shall consider it at leisure."
translations.idiomatic: Then he added: "I will think on it."

sentences.zh: 數日，詔降為東海郡侯。

translations.literal: 」Several days later, an edict demoted him to Marquis of Donghai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Days later an edict demoted him to Marquis of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 大元游騎至高橋，宰臣以聞。

translations.literal: Great Yuan raiding cavalry reached Gaoqiao; the chief ministers reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol raiders reached Gaoqiao, and the chief ministers reported it.

sentences.zh: 宣宗使人問執中，執中曰：「計畫已定矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong sent someone to ask Zhizhong; Zhizhong said: "The plan is already settled."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong sent to ask Zhizhong, who replied: "The plan is already set."

sentences.zh: 既而讓宰執曰：「吾為尚書令，豈得不先與議而遽奏耶？」

translations.literal: 」Then he reproached the chief executives, saying: "I am Director of the Masters in the Secretariat — how could you report urgently without discussing it with me first?"
translations.idiomatic: He then reproached the chief ministers: "As Director of the Masters in the Secretariat, how could you report to me without consulting me first?"

sentences.zh: 宰執遜謝而已。

translations.literal: 」The chief executives merely yielded and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers could only apologize.

sentences.zh: 提點近侍局慶山奴、副使惟弼、奉御惟康請除執中，宣宗念援立功，隱忍不許。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Palace Attendants Bureau Qingshannu, deputy commissioner Weibi, and palace attendant Weikang requested dismissal of Zhizhong; Emperor Xuanzong, mindful of his merit in enthroning him, forbore and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Qingshannu, commissioner of the Palace Attendants Bureau, Deputy Commissioner Weibi, and Palace Attendant Weikang asked that Zhizhong be removed. Mindful of his service in enthroning him, Emperor Xuanzong held back and refused.

sentences.zh: 元帥右監軍術虎高琪屢戰不利，執中戒之曰：「今日出兵果無功，當以軍法從事矣。」

translations.literal: Right supervising commander of the Marshalate Shuhu Gaoqi repeatedly fought without success; Zhizhong warned him: "If today's deployment truly brings no merit, military law will be applied."
translations.idiomatic: Shuhu Gaoqi, right supervising commander of the marshalate, had lost repeatedly. Zhizhong warned him: "If today's sortie fails again, you will answer to military law."

sentences.zh: 高琪出戰復敗，自度不免，頗聞慶山奴諸人有謀，十月辛亥，高琪遂率所將颭軍入中都，圍執中第。

translations.literal: 」Gaoqi went out to battle and was defeated again; judging himself beyond escape, having heard that Qingshannu and the others had a plot, on xinhai of the tenth month Gaoqi then led the Zhan troops under his command into the Central Capital and besieged Zhizhong's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi fought again and lost. Concluding he could not escape, and hearing that Qingshannu and others were plotting against him, on xinhai of the tenth month he marched his Zhan troops into the Central Capital and surrounded Zhizhong's mansion.

sentences.zh: 執中聞變，彎弓注矢外射，不勝，登後垣欲走，衣絓墮而傷股，軍士就斬之。

translations.literal: Zhizhong heard of the disturbance, bent his bow and aimed arrows outward, could not prevail, climbed the rear wall intending to flee, but his garment caught and he fell, injuring his thigh; soldiers came up and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Alerted to the mutiny, Zhizhong strung his bow and shot at the assailants but could not hold them off. He climbed the rear wall to flee, caught his robe, fell and injured his thigh, and soldiers cut him down.

sentences.zh: 高琪持執中首詣闕待罪，宣宗赦之。

translations.literal: Gaoqi carried Zhizhong's head to the palace to await punishment; Emperor Xuanzong pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqi brought Zhizhong's head to court to accept punishment. Emperor Xuanzong pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 以為左副元帥。

translations.literal: He was made left vice marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qi was made left vice marshal.

sentences.zh: 執中之党呼于衢路曰：「颭軍反矣，殺之者有賞。」

translations.literal: Zhizhong's faction shouted in the streets: "The Zhan troops have rebelled — whoever kills them will be rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong's partisans cried in the streets: "The Zhan troops have rebelled! Kill them and be rewarded!"

sentences.zh: 市人從之。

translations.literal: 」Market people followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Townspeople joined in.

sentences.zh: 颭軍死者甚眾，一軍皆恟恟，宣宗遣近侍撫諭之，詔有司量加賻贈，眾乃稍安。

translations.literal: Very many Zhan troops died; the whole army was in uproar; Emperor Xuanzong dispatched close attendants to comfort and instruct them, and edicted the relevant offices to add burial grants according to measure, and the crowd then gradually calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Many Zhan soldiers were killed and the entire corps was in turmoil. Emperor Xuanzong sent close attendants to reassure them and ordered appropriate burial grants; the men gradually settled.

sentences.zh: 明日，除特末也泰甯軍節度使，烏古論奮剌真授知濟南府事，徒單金壽真授知歸德府事，蒲察六斤真授知平陽府事。

translations.literal: The next day, Temo ye was appointed Military Commissioner of the Taining Army; Ugulian Fenla was truly appointed to know the affairs of Jinan Prefecture; Tudan Jinshou was truly appointed to know the affairs of Guide Prefecture; Pucha Liujin was truly appointed to know the affairs of Pingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Temo ye was made military commissioner of the Taining Army; Ugulian Duola was formally installed as prefect of Jinan; Tudan Jinshou as prefect of Guide; and Pucha Liujin as prefect of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，左諫議大夫張行信上封事曰：「《春秋》之法，國君立不以道，若嘗與諸侯盟會，即列為諸侯。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Left Remonstrance Grandee Zhang Xingxin submitted a sealed memorial saying: "The method of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that when a ruler is enthroned not by the proper way, if he has once joined in covenant with the feudal lords, he is ranked among the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Left Remonstrance Grandee Zhang Xingxin submitted a sealed memorial: "The Spring and Autumn Annals hold that a ruler enthroned by improper means, if he has ever entered into league with the feudal lords, is listed among them.

sentences.zh: 東海在位已六年矣，為其臣者誰敢幹之。

translations.literal: Donghai has held the throne already six years; as his ministers, who would dare interfere?
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Donghai reigned six years — which of his ministers would have dared challenge him?

sentences.zh: 胡沙虎握兵入城，躬行弑逆，當是時惟鄯陽、石古乃率眾赴援，至於戰死，論其忠烈，在朝食祿者皆當愧之。

translations.literal: Hu Shahu seized troops and entered the city, personally carrying out regicide; at that time only Shanyang and Shigunai led the masses to rush to aid, going so far as to die in battle — considering their loyalty and heroism, those who held salary at court ought all to feel ashamed before them.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shahu marched into the city and murdered the emperor himself. Only Shanyang and Shigunai rallied men to his defense and died fighting. Measured against their loyalty, every salaried official at court should hang his head in shame.

sentences.zh: 陛下始親萬機，海內望化，褒顯二人，延及子孫，庶幾少慰貞魂，激天下之義氣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has just begun personally to attend to the myriad affairs of state; within the seas all look for transformation — to commend and display these two men and extend it to their descendants would perhaps slightly comfort their steadfast souls and stir the spirit of righteousness throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has just taken the reins; the realm looks to you for reform. Honor these two men and extend the favor to their descendants — that would comfort their loyal spirits and rouse the world's sense of duty.

sentences.zh: 宋徐羨之、傅亮、謝晦弑營陽王立文帝，文帝誅之，以江陵奉迎之誠，免其妻子。

translations.literal: In Song, Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and Xie Hui assassinated Prince Yingyang and enthroned Emperor Wen; Emperor Wen executed them, yet because of their sincere welcome at Jiangling, spared their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: In the Song, Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and Xie Hui killed Prince Yingyang and enthroned Emperor Wen. Wen executed them but spared their families for the sincerity with which they had welcomed him at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 胡沙虎國之大賊，世所共惡，雖已死而罪名未正，合暴其過惡，宣佈中外，除名削爵，緣坐其家，然後為快。

translations.literal: Hu Shahu is the state's great villain, hated by all the world together; though already dead his crime has not been rectified — it is fitting to expose his errors and wickedness, proclaim them within and without, remove his name and strip his rank, implicate his household by association, and only then be satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shahu was the realm's great traitor, hated by all. Though dead, his guilt has not been settled. Expose his crimes, proclaim them throughout the realm, erase his name, strip his titles, and punish his household — only then will justice be done.

sentences.zh: 陛下若不忍援立之勞，則依仿元嘉故事，亦足以示懲戒。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty cannot bear to forget the labor of enthroning him, then following the precedent of the Yuanjia era would also suffice to show warning and restraint."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty cannot forget his service in putting you on the throne, the Yuanjia precedent would still serve as sufficient warning."

sentences.zh: 宣宗乃下詔暴執中過惡，削其官爵。

translations.literal: 」Emperor Xuanzong then issued an edict exposing Zhizhong's errors and wickedness and stripping his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong then issued an edict denouncing Zhizhong's crimes and stripping his rank.

sentences.zh: 贈鄯陽、石古乃，加恩其子。

translations.literal: Shanyang and Shigunai were posthumously rewarded, and favor was added to their sons.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang and Shigunai were posthumously honored, and their sons were rewarded.

sentences.zh: 慶山奴、惟弼、惟康皆遷賞，近侍局自此用事矣。

translations.literal: Qingshannu, Weibi, and Weikang were all transferred and rewarded; from this the Palace Attendants Bureau began to wield power.
translations.idiomatic: Qingshannu, Weibi, and Weikang were all promoted and rewarded — from then on the Palace Attendants Bureau held the reins of power.

sentences.zh: 論曰：金九主，遇弑者三，其逆謀者十人。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Of the Jin's nine rulers, three met assassination; those who plotted rebellion numbered ten men.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Of the Jin's nine emperors, three were murdered; ten men plotted regicide.

sentences.zh: 熙宗之弑，惟大興國一人世宗聲其罪而磔之思陵之側。

translations.literal: In the assassination of Emperor Xizong, of Daxingguo alone did Emperor Shizong proclaim his crime and dismember him beside Siling.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong was murdered, only Daxingguo was singled out by Emperor Shizong, who proclaimed his guilt and had him dismembered beside Siling.

sentences.zh: 徒單貞雖誅。

translations.literal: Tudan Zhen, though executed,
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Zhen was executed,

sentences.zh: 未聞暴其罪狀，後以戚畹又復贈官追封。

translations.literal: there was never heard exposing of his crimes; later, because of imperial affinal kinship, he was again given posthumous office and pursued ennoblement.
translations.idiomatic: yet his crimes were never publicly exposed; later, as an imperial in-law, he was again ennobled and posthumously promoted.

sentences.zh: 余秉德、唐括辯等六人，皆以他罪誅，海陵之弑，其首惡為完顏元宜，則令終焉。

translations.literal: Yu Bingde, Tangguo Bian, and six others were all executed on other charges; in Hailing's assassination, the chief villain was Wanyan Yuanyi — yet he died a natural end.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bingde, Tangguo Bian, and four others were all executed on other charges. In Hailing's murder the ringleader was Wanyan Yuanyi — who died peacefully in bed.

sentences.zh: 衛紹王之弑曰胡沙虎，不死于司敗之誅，而死于高琪之手。

translations.literal: The assassin of Prince Shao of Wei was called Hu Shahu — he did not die by execution under the Director of Punishments, but died at Gao Qi's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shao of Wei's murderer was Hu Shahu. He did not die by lawful execution but was killed privately by Gao Qi.

sentences.zh: 古所謂弑君之賊人得而討之者，謂請於公上而致討焉。

translations.literal: What antiquity called "the regicide whom anyone may punish" means petitioning the sovereign to carry out the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that anyone may punish a ruler's murderer — meaning by petitioning the throne to execute justice.

sentences.zh: 如孔子之請討陳恆是也。

translations.literal: Confucius's request to punish Chen Heng is a case in point.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius demanding punishment for Chen Heng is the model.

sentences.zh: 豈有如琪之擅殺而以為功者乎。

translations.literal: How could there be one like Qi who killed on his own authority and counted it merit?
translations.idiomatic: How different from Qi, who killed on his own authority and was rewarded for it!

sentences.zh: 金之政刑，其亂若此，國欲不亡，其可得乎！

translations.literal: The Jin's governance and punishments were in such disorder — if the state wished not to perish, could that be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: When governance and justice had fallen so far, how could the Jin hope to survive?
